TO: DER Program Manager
CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DATE: 07/01/2025
SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking

1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.

/s/
Harriet Ngoyi
Director, Regulatory Affairs
Alleniom Utilities

§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.
This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.


--- page 2 ---
§2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:
(1)  Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
the affected site.
(2)  An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
exception).
(3)  The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.
Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).
§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.
The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.
Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.
The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.
Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.
Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.


--- page 3 ---
§4 TIMELINES
Timelines below run from the date on which Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11
to Distribution Protection Engineering. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays.

Classification is made by the Manager, Distribution Protection Engineering, on receipt of Form ER-11.
Where the reviewer requests reclassification, the request is decided in writing within two business days.
Extensions to the timelines above are permitted only in writing, are issued by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and are copied to the DER Program Manager and Regulatory Affairs. Applications
shall not be held in queue pending revision of a standard where this procedure provides a determination
path; extensions do not authorize a screening hold outside this procedure.
§5 DOCUMENTATION
The completed Form ER-11, the engineering determination, and any supporting studies are filed with the
application record retained by Interconnection Studies for the retention period established by Regulatory
Affairs. A copy of the completed Form ER-11 is filed in the Standards Engineering ERP-9 register of
per-site determinations.
The ERP-9 register records, at minimum: the referral number, the receipt date, the Project ID, the site type
and feeder, the standards documents at issue, the assigned engineer, the determination date, and a short
summary of the determination. The register is reviewed by Standards Engineering quarterly for recurring
patterns; where a pattern warrants a standards revision proposal, Standards Engineering initiates that
revision separately from, and in parallel with, ongoing per-site determinations under this procedure. A
pending revision proposal does not stay determinations issued under this procedure and does not
authorize a screening hold on affected applications.
Determinations issued under ERP-9 are cited in the interconnection service agreement (ISA) drafted for
the affected site by reference to the ER-11 referral number and determination date. Modifications to the
site's protection arrangement subsequent to ISA execution are handled under the change-order provisions
of the executed ISA, subject to DIS-01 §7 where capacity or POI is affected.

§1  SCOPE
This guideline governs deployment sequencing of constrained utility equipment (RTUs, reclosers) across
completed sites awaiting energization. It applies to Alleniom-owned devices installed by Distribution
Operations for the purpose of energizing a construction-complete distributed energy resource (DER) site,
when supplier lead times or quarterly delivery quantities constrain the number of sites that can be
equipped in a given deployment window.
This guideline does NOT apply to application processing. Nondiscriminatory queue-order treatment of
interconnection applications is governed by Interconnection Tariff §12.7 and by the procedures
administered by Interconnection Studies; nothing in this guideline modifies, displaces, or supplements
those procedures. The rankings established under §2 operate solely on sites for which interconnection
application processing is complete, the interconnection agreement (where required) is executed, and
construction is certified complete by the customer or its contractor.
Devices out of scope: customer-owned protective equipment; utility-owned equipment already installed at
the site; distribution-system reinforcement equipment scheduled under an approved capital work order.
Program scope for the underlying DER remains as defined in DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Interconnection Tariff
§12.2.
§2  COMMISSIONING CRITICALITY
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
As a general rule, deployment priority for constrained equipment follows interconnection queue order,
consistent with the nondiscriminatory treatment principles of Interconnection Tariff §12.7.
A site may be advanced ahead of queue order under certain circumstances — the urgent nature of a
request, in particular for public infrastructure (schools, hospitals, water/wastewater facilities), or an
expedited deployment pathway on reasonable customer request — but only where substantiated by the
site's own recorded attributes (per §3), in order of priority: (1) essential-service function (water/wastewater,
emergency, health); (2) committed in-service or grant-funding deadline; (3) construction-complete date.
Among sites of the same critical nature, the deciding factor is interconnection queue order; requests not
substantiated by these attributes remain in queue order.


--- page 2 ---
OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline
Page 2
Factor definitions:
•
Essential-service function. A site whose primary served load is a public water or wastewater facility;
a hospital, emergency-response, or first-responder facility; or a public-health facility for which loss of
service is treated as an emergency by the responsible jurisdiction. Essential-service status is
evidenced by the customer's facility classification of record and, where applicable, the served-load
designation on the interconnection application.
•
Committed in-service or grant-funding deadline. A contractually committed in-service date, or a
date on which grant funding lapses if the site is not in service, established in a fully executed written
instrument between the customer and a governmental funder, project sponsor, or off-taker. Internal
customer construction targets, marketing dates, budget-cycle expectations, and school-year,
fiscal-year, or seasonal preferences do not constitute a committed deadline under this factor.
•
Construction-complete date. The calendar date on which the customer's construction of the site
was certified complete and ready for utility energization steps. Where more than one date is recorded,
the earlier of (a) the customer's written notice of construction completion and (b) the utility's on-site
verification, controls.
•
Queue date as tiebreaker. The interconnection queue date of the site's underlying application, used
only to break a tie among sites that rank equally on factors (1), (2), and (3).
External advocacy, correspondence volume, elected-official inquiries, and stakeholder communications
received in relation to a site do not enter the ranking. Ranking is determined from the raw attributes above,
evidenced by the source documents in §3.
§3  DOCUMENTATION
For each deployment window the DER Program Office shall assemble a deployment worksheet listing
every site meeting the eligibility conditions of §1, with the following fields drawn from the identified system
of record:
•
Site name and interconnection application ID (DER Program queue).
•
Customer / party of record and site service address (DER Program queue).
•
Nameplate capacity and program-scope classification per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (application file).
•
Devices required to energize (RTU, POI recloser, or both), quantities, and specification references
(Standards Engineering).
•
Construction-complete date and source of certification (project construction file).
•
Contracted in-service or grant-funding deadline, if any, with the executed instrument establishing it
attached by reference (customer submission).
•
Essential-service classification, if any, with the customer's facility classification of record attached by
reference (application file).
•
Interconnection queue date (DER Program queue).
The worksheet shall record the §2 factor on which each ranked site qualifies. Sites that do not qualify at
ranks (1) or (2) are ranked by (3) with (4) as tiebreaker. The worksheet, the ranked deployment list, and
the assigned equipment-set identifiers shall be retained in the DER Program equipment-planning file for
the applicable window and provided to the SOC concurrent with the coordination step described in §5.

§1   Purpose
This procedure defines the supplemental review process applied to distributed energy resource (DER)
interconnection applications that fail one or more of the fast-track technical screens set out in the Alleniom DER
Interconnection Standard (DIS-01 Rev 4). It establishes the ordered screens, data sources, and documentation to
be produced by the interconnection engineer conducting supplemental review, and identifies the conditions under
which a study agreement is required before the application may proceed.
Supplemental review is intended to allow an application that fails an initial fast-track screen to be evaluated
against a bounded set of additional technical criteria without incurring the cost and schedule of a full system
impact study, where that evaluation can be completed from existing feeder data and standard engineering
judgment.
Nothing in this procedure alters the substantive interconnection standards contained in DIS-01, the protection
requirements contained in DPS-07, or the telemetry and communications requirements contained in TCS-02.
§2   Scope
This procedure applies to:
(a)  all in-scope DER interconnection applications (≥500 kW) as defined in DIS-01 §3 that have entered
supplemental review following failure of an initial screen; and
(b)  all DER classes recognized in DIS-01 §3 — commercial small-scale (500 kW – 1 MW) and medium-scale (1
MW – 5 MW).
This procedure does not apply to:
(a)  sub-500 kW installations processed under the Simplified Small-Systems Process;
(b)  capacity or point-of-interconnection changes to an executed interconnection service agreement, which are
governed by DIS-01 §7; or
(c)  domestic rooftop solar, which is out of scope for the DER Program.
Where a supplemental-review screen result is inconclusive on the record before the engineer, the application shall
be advanced to a study agreement rather than passed or failed under this procedure.
§3   Screens


--- page 2 ---
SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering
Page 2
Applications entering supplemental review shall be evaluated under the following screens, in the order given. An
application that fails any screen shall be considered a candidate for a study agreement; the reviewing engineer
shall document the failing screen, the underlying data, and the recommended disposition per §6.
Screen A — Aggregate DER penetration on the feeder. Total nameplate DER (existing plus queued plus
requested) on the subject feeder shall not exceed the applicable penetration threshold set in DIS-01. Queue
positions are those on record with the DER Program Office at the date of screen evaluation.
Screen B — Voltage regulation and flicker. Reviewed against the feeder's most recent planning study or, where
none is on file for the subject feeder within twenty-four (24) months, against a screening voltage-rise calculation
performed using conductor and transformer impedance from the distribution planning record.
Screen C — Short-circuit contribution. DER short-circuit contribution shall not cause any feeder-protective
device to exceed 87.5% of its interrupting rating, nor cause any downstream protection coordination margin to
fall below the values specified in DPS-07.
Screen D — 100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. Governed by §4.
Screen E — Reverse power flow at substation. Where the aggregate DER on the subject feeder exceeds the
substation transformer's certified reverse-power capability, or where reverse-power protective settings are not in
place, the application shall be routed to study.
Passing all applicable screens is a necessary but not sufficient condition for interconnection; the application
remains subject to the balance of the DIS-01 evaluation, including protection and telemetry requirements.
§4   100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. For solar DER, the minimum load used in this screen shall be the
minimum load within the daytime window 10:00–16:00, determined from feeder AMI interval data. The absolute
overnight minimum shall NOT be used. Requested DER capacity must be ≤ this daytime-window minimum for
the site to pass the screen.
The daytime-window minimum shall be computed from feeder AMI interval data covering the most recent
complete twelve (12) calendar months, aggregated to fifteen-minute intervals aligned to the feeder AMI
collection cadence, and evaluated only over intervals whose start time falls within 10:00–16:00 local clock time
on the feeder. Intervals affected by known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching shall be excluded
and the exclusion documented in the reviewer's worksheet. Where fewer than twelve (12) months of AMI interval
data are available, the reviewer shall use the longest continuous complete period available and note the
data-window length in the supplemental review memo.
The daytime-window minimum determined under this section is the sole minimum-load figure used for the solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen. Feeder minimum-load figures produced for other purposes — planning studies,
hosting-capacity map inputs, protection coordination — are not substitutes for the value computed under this
section and shall not be carried into the Screen D determination without recomputation on the AMI record.
Where a prior supplemental review memo on the same feeder has applied a different minimum-load basis, the
reviewer shall recompute the value under this section and, if the two disagree, supersede the earlier memo in the
file.
§5   Data sources
The following data sources are authoritative for supplemental review under this procedure:


--- page 3 ---
SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering
Page 3
(a)  Feeder AMI interval data — from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse, at the meter aggregation level
published for the subject feeder. AMI interval data is the sole authoritative source for the Screen D
minimum-load determination described in §4.
(b)  Distribution planning record — most recent feeder planning study, conductor and transformer impedance
data, and protection coordination settings, held by Distribution Planning.
(c)  DER queue — active-queue and on-hold registers maintained by the DER Program Office as of the screen
evaluation date. Queue entries not yet reflected in a published hosting-capacity map remain applicable to Screen
A.
(d)  Certified Equipment List (CEL) — current edition, for verification that proposed inverters and PCS
equipment are eligible to be considered under the screens.
(e)  Interconnection application record — the applicant's filed capacity, single-line diagram, inverter
specifications, and control narrative (where controlled-capacity operation is asserted under DIS-01 §3.6).
Substitution of a source not listed above shall be documented in the memo produced under §6, together with the
reason for the substitution.
§6   Documentation
The reviewing engineer shall produce a supplemental review memo for each application processed under this
procedure. The memo shall contain, at minimum:
(a)  application identifier, applicant, subject feeder, and requested capacity;
(b)  the screens applied and the pass/fail determination for each;
(c)  for Screen D, the daytime-window minimum load determined per §4, the data window used, the count of
intervals evaluated, and any interval exclusions with reason;
(d)  the recommended disposition — advance without study agreement, advance to study agreement, or return to
applicant with specified deficiency;
(e)  reviewer signature and date; and
(f)  the identifiers of any earlier supplemental review memos superseded.

Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy
Applies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.
Supersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).
Owner:  DER Program Office.
Approving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.

§1  Purpose
This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
(a)applications are closed only on a documented basis;
(b)queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
(c)staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
(d)the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
§2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§2.1  Scope of §2
This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
(a)the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
(b)the customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or
(c)a new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.
§2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation
To constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:
(a)be from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);
(b)be received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;
(c)identify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and
(d)state expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.
Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
§2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)
Where staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:
1.Confirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;
2.Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
3.Log the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;
4.On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and
5.Preserve the withdrawal writing in the case file in accordance with §4.
Absent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.
§2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site
Where a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:
(a)The DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. No queue-date inheritance is permitted between the prior and the new application.
(b)The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
(c)The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.
(d)Where the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.
§2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6
Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
§3.1  Relationship to the Tariff
This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.
§3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice
The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
(a)the application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;
(b)at least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and
(c)the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
§3.3  Form and Service of the Notice
Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
(a)be issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;
(b)be served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;
(c)identify the application by identifier and site;
(d)state the item(s) requiring response;
(e)state the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; and
(f)state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
§3.4  Computation of 30 Business Days
For purposes of this §3 and of tariff §12.4:
(a)“Business days” excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal legal public holidays observed within the response window;
(b)Day 1 is the first business day after the date of issuance stated on the notice;
(c)The following federal holidays observed within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized as non-business days and are not counted:
Holiday | Observed Date
Memorial Day | 05/26/2025
Juneteenth National Independence Day | 06/19/2025
Independence Day | 07/04/2025


(d)Where a response window straddles a federal holiday not listed above, the case handler shall exclude that holiday from the count and document the calculation in the case file.
§3.5  Effect of Non-Response
If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. The DER Program Office shall:
(a)mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
(b)record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and
(c)preserve the notice, proof of service, and the closure entry in the case file in accordance with §4.
§3.6  Effect of Timely Response
A substantive response received on or before expiration of the 30 business-day window suspends the deemed-withdrawal consequence. The case handler shall evaluate the response and, if the identified matter is cured, release the application to resume processing. If the response is non-substantive or does not cure the identified matter, the case handler shall so document and, if warranted, issue a further follow-up or a subsequent Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation.
§3.7  Non-Substitution
Issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation is not a substitute for the customer-request path under §2, and the customer-request path under §2 is not a substitute for the deemed-withdrawal path under §3. Case handlers shall not use one mechanism to accomplish what should be effected under the other.
§4  Record-Keeping Requirements
§4.1  Case File Contents
For every application closed under §2 or §3, the DER Program Office shall maintain a case file containing, at minimum:
(a)the original application and all completeness/acknowledgement communications;
(b)for §2 closures: the writing (letter or email) requesting official withdrawal confirmation from the applicant; the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation (letter or email) as received; and any related correspondence bearing on the applicant's intent to withdraw;
(c)for §3 closures: the prior follow-up correspondence relied upon under §3.2(b); the Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation as issued; proof of service (certified mail receipt or verified electronic delivery record); the 30 business-day computation worksheet; and any respo

Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.

/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:31:Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:35:2.Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:37:4.On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and

/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:43:(b)The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:44:(c)The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. /tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:47:Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:48:§3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:49:Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:51:This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. /tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:53:The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:56:(c)the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:58:Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:64:(f)state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:78:If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. /tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:79:(a)mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:80:(b)record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and
/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Standards/Queue_Management_Withdrawal_Policy.docx.txt:83:A substantive response received on or before expiration of the 30 business-day window suspends the deemed-withdrawal consequence. ---
name: workplace-apps
description: How to work with the project applications a task exposes through MCP servers (mail, calendar, spreadsheets, documents, PDFs, file storage, project trackers such as OpenProject, wikis, databases, CAD) - discover tools, read records, create or update items, and confirm the change took effect. Use when the task mentions an application, a work package, ticket, email, meeting, wiki page or database, or when MCP servers are listed.
---

# Workplace applications over MCP

## Discover
- List the servers and their tools once; save the tool list to `/tmp/ahpele/mcp_tools.md` with one line per tool
  (name: purpose, required arguments) so you do not need to list them again.
- Prefer read/search/list tools to explore; note IDs (project, work package type, status, user) you will need.

## Read the record
- Search mail and documents by project identifiers, names and dates; read full threads, attachments and their dates.
- The record "as of" a date excludes anything dated later.
- Keep a dated timeline and a list of sources (application, item id, title, date) for citations.

## Create or update
- Before creating, check whether a suitable item already exists, and the required fields (project, type, subject,
  description, assignee, status, dates, priority, custom fields).
- Put the substance in the item: the determination, each open item with its owner and due date, and references to the
  documents it rests on. Keep it consistent with any memo or file you deliver.
- Use the exact project, list or folder the instruction names.

## Confirm
- After every create/update, read the item back and verify the fields are stored as intended. If a call fails, read the
  error, fix the arguments and retry; do not assume success.
- Mention every created or updated item (application, id, title) in your final message.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue

1. Determination
 NO — PTO CANNOT ISSUE ON 08/04/2025 ON THE RECORD AS IT
 STANDS.
Permission to Operate cannot issue for Corwyn Office Complex PV on 08/04/2025 on the
record before me. The customer's SWBD-PV main breaker is rated 1,200 A on a 750 kVA
transformer whose 480 V secondary full-load current is 902 A. That is 133% of the
transformer secondary current; the strict secondary-protection limit in NFPA 70-2023 Table
450.3(A) is 125% (1,127.6 A) unless the transformer is documented as supervised, and a
next-higher standard rating is available only on a written code basis. The record contains no
supervised-transformer basis, no written next-higher-standard basis, no signed design
determination on the point, and no AHJ acceptance of either basis. The City of Wrenford's
final approval of 07/02/2025 and the completed witness test do not cure this.
The witness test, inverter certification and telemetry record are otherwise in order for the
inverter protective functions. The blocking item is the customer's transformer secondary
protection, which must be corrected or documented before the facility is energized. A
separate pre-issuance check of the Certified Equipment List edition in force on 08/04/2025
(CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025) is also required; it is not a present non-
conformance but it must be closed before issuance.

are met: (i) the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted; (ii) telemetry is live at
the System Operations Center; (iii) the witness test is complete; and (iv) the authority
having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities. Article 4.1 also
requires the Facility to conform to DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's

3. What stands in the way: F-1 — SWBD-PV main breaker against
the T-1 secondary protection limit
F-1. The SWBD-PV main breaker is not verified against the T-1 secondary
overcurrent-protection limit.
Requirement. NFPA 70-2023, Table 450.3(A) (adopted by the City of Wrenford by Ordinance
24-118 and made part of permit WEP-25-0317), limits the secondary overcurrent device for
a transformer over 1,000 V to 125% of the transformer secondary full-load current; the
250% column applies only where the transformer is supervised. ISA Article 4.1 requires the
Facility to conform to the Company standards and the code in effect, and ISA Article 6.2
requires the AHJ's final approval of the customer's facilities.
What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, dated 06/24/2025: the T-1 row states
750 kVA, 13.2 kV to 480Y/277 V and a full-load secondary current of 902 A; the SWBD-PV
row states a 1,200 A bus and a 1,200 A main breaker. The calculation is 902 A × 1.25 =
1,127.6 A. The installed 1,200 A main is 133% of 902 A and 72.4 A (6.4%) above the 125%
value. The record has no supervised-transformer designation, no signed supervision basis,
and no AHJ finding on the point. The 07/02/2025 Certificate of Final Approval records the
inspection result but does not document this check.
Conclusion. On the strict, non-supervised reading of Table 450.3(A) — the reading I apply
because the record does not establish supervision — the 1,200 A main exceeds the 125%
secondary limit. I therefore cannot verify the T-1 secondary protection as designed. This is a
hold item, not a documentation comment. If Corwyn contends that the next-higher standard
rating is permitted, it must put the code basis and the AHJ's written acceptance on the
record; the record as it stands does not contain either.
What has to be done. Corwyn Realty Partners, through its contractor Brantley Electric
Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must do one of the following:
  (a) Replace the SWBD-PV main breaker with a standard 1,000 A breaker (1,000 A / 902 A
   = 111%, within 125%), update the equipment schedule and the arc-flash label, and
   obtain re-inspection and final approval from the City of Wrenford; or
 (b) Provide a signed supervised-transformer basis acceptable to the City of Wrenford
   under Table 450.3(A), with the AHJ's written acceptance, and update the record
   accordingly; or
 (c) Provide the written code basis, and the City of Wrenford's written acceptance, for
   using the next-higher standard rating under Table 450.3(A) (1,200 A is the next standard
   rating above 1,127.6 A), and update the record accordingly. The record as it stands
   contains none of (a), (b) or (c).
The replacement breaker must be rated for the 15.7 kA available fault current and the 35 kA
switchboard rating, and the busbar check must remain satisfied: five 225 A inverter
breakers plus the 40 A TX-1 breaker = 1,165 A, which is within the 1,200 A bus. The revised
equipment schedule, breaker rating and AHJ re-approval must be provided to the DER

=== memo text
[1] Heading 1: 1. Determination
[2] Normal: Permission to Operate cannot issue for Corwyn Office Complex PV on 08/04/2025 on the record before me. The customer's SWBD-PV main breaker is rated 1,200 A on a 750 kVA transformer whose 480 V secondary full-load current is 902 A. That is 133% of the transformer secondary current; the strict secondary-protection limit in NFPA 70-2023 Table 450.3(A) is 125% (1,127.6 A) unless the transformer is documented as supervised, and a next-higher standard rating is available only on a written code basis. The record contains no supervised-transformer basis, no written next-higher-standard basis, no signed design determination on the point, and no AHJ acceptance of either basis. The City of Wrenford's final approval of 07/02/2025 and the completed witness test do not cure this.
[3] Normal: The witness test, inverter certification and telemetry record are otherwise in order for the inverter protective functions. The blocking item is the customer's transformer secondary protection, which must be corrected or documented before the facility is energized. A separate pre-issuance check of the Certified Equipment List edition in force on 08/04/2025 (CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025) is also required; it is not a present non-conformance but it must be closed before issuance.
[4] Heading 1: 2. Basis: the ISA conditions and the record at 07/14/2025
[5] Normal: ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, Article 6.2, permits parallel operation only once four conditions are met: (i) the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted; (ii) telemetry is live at the System Operations Center; (iii) the witness test is complete; and (iv) the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities. Article 4.1 also requires the Facility to conform to DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's Certified Equipment List, each as in effect from time to time. I checked each condition against the record as of 07/14/2025.
[6] Normal: The four matters placed under separate review are not decided here: (1) the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser; (2) the POI recloser settings and the protection coordination study; (3) the site's queue position; and (4) the system impact study and its conditions. The checklist's entries for (1) and (2) are recorded as complete/accepted/issued on 07/08/2025 and 06/18/2025; I have not re-reviewed the underlying tests, settings or study. Nothing else is outside this memo.
[7] Heading 1: 3. What stands in the way: F-1 — SWBD-PV main breaker against the T-1 secondary protection limit
[8] Normal: F-1. The SWBD-PV main breaker is not verified against the T-1 secondary overcurrent-protection limit.
[9] Normal: Requirement. NFPA 70-2023, Table 450.3(A) (adopted by the City of Wrenford by Ordinance 24-118 and made part of permit WEP-25-0317), limits the secondary overcurrent device for a transformer over 1,000 V to 125% of the transformer secondary full-load current; the 250% column applies only where the transformer is supervised. ISA Article 4.1 requires the Facility to conform to the Company standards and the code in effect, and ISA Article 6.2 requires the AHJ's final approval of the customer's facilities.
[10] Normal: What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, dated 06/24/2025: the T-1 row states 750 kVA, 13.2 kV to 480Y/277 V and a full-load secondary current of 902 A; the SWBD-PV row states a 1,200 A bus and a 1,200 A main breaker. The calculation is 902 A × 1.25 = 1,127.6 A. The installed 1,200 A main is 133% of 902 A and 72.4 A (6.4%) above the 125% value. The record has no supervised-transformer designation, no signed supervision basis, no written next-higher-standard basis, and no AHJ finding specifically addressing the 125%/next-higher basis. The 07/02/2025 Certificate of Final Approval records the inspection result but does not document this check.
[11] Normal: Conclusion. On the strict, non-supervised reading of Table 450.3(A) — the reading I apply because the record does not establish supervision — the 1,200 A main exceeds the 125% secondary limit. I therefore cannot verify the T-1 secondary protection as designed. This is a hold item, not a documentation comment. If Corwyn contends that the next-higher standard rating is permitted, it must put the code basis and the AHJ's written acceptance on the record; the record as it stands does not contain either.
[12] Normal: What has to be done. Corwyn Realty Partners, through its contractor Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must do one of the following:
[13] List Bullet: (a) Replace the SWBD-PV main breaker with a standard 1,000 A breaker (1,000 A / 902 A = 111%, within 125%), update the equipment schedule and the arc-flash label, and obtain re-inspection and final approval from the City of Wrenford; or
[14] List Bullet: (b) Provide a signed supervised-transformer basis acceptable to the City of Wrenford under Table 450.3(A), with the AHJ's written acceptance, and update the record accordingly; or
[15] List Bullet: (c) Provide the written code basis, and the City of Wrenford's written acceptance, for using the next-higher standard rating under Table 450.3(A) (1,200 A is the next standard rating above 1,127.6 A), and update the record accordingly. The record as it stands contains none of (a), (b) or (c).
[16] Normal: The replacement breaker must be rated for the 15.7 kA available fault current and the 35 kA switchboard rating, and the busbar check must remain satisfied: five 225 A inverter breakers plus the 40 A TX-1 breaker = 1,165 A, which is within the 1,200 A bus. The revised equipment schedule, breaker rating and AHJ re-approval must be provided to the DER Program Office before PTO.
[17] Normal: Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor) for the design, breaker, code basis and AHJ submission; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for re-inspection and final approval; the DER Program Office for verification. Distribution Protection Engineering's POI settings and coordination study remain outside this memo; the DER Program Office will notify DPE of the corrected customer-side record for information only.
[18] Normal: Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Not on the record. As of 07/14/2025 there is no revised drawing, no breaker order or availability confirmation, no signed supervision/next-higher basis, and no AHJ re-inspection booked; the 07/02/2025 final approval is for the 1,200 A design. A 1,000 A breaker and a re-inspection, or a written code/AHJ basis, may be achievable in the time available, but the record does not demonstrate it. To keep 08/04/2025, Corwyn must complete (a), (b) or (c) and deliver the AHJ acceptance to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025. Otherwise PTO should be held and re-determined when the corrected record is complete. The witness test remains valid; the correction does not require re-testing the inverter protective functions.
[19] Heading 1: 4. Pre-issuance confirmations (to be closed before PTO, not present non-conformances)
[20] Normal: C-1. CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025.
[21] Normal: ISA Article 4.1 requires conformity with the Certified Equipment List as in effect from time to time. CEL-2025-Q2 (04/30/2025) lists VX-140C at row 18 and is the edition checked on the 07/14/2025 checklist. CEL-2025-Q2 states that CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025, before the requested PTO date. Evan Solberg, Standards Engineering, is to confirm in writing by 08/01/2025 that VX-140C remains listed on the CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025. If it is delisted, the facility cannot be verified against the current CEL and PTO must be held and re-determined; if it remains listed, this condition is closed. This confirmation can be completed by 08/01/2025.
[22] Normal: C-2. Live telemetry at the moment of PTO.
[23] Normal: TCS-02 §5 and ISA Articles 6.2 and 7.2 require live telemetry at the SOC when PTO is issued, with the SOC Shift Supervisor's confirmation recorded against the file. The checklist records the 07/08/2025 confirmation by L. Kovalchuk, and the 07/14/2025 SOC PTO-Hold Log has no Corwyn entry. Lena Kovalchuk/SOC is to re-confirm at the moment of issuance on 08/04/2025 that all required points are valid (not stale, forced or bad-quality) at the SCADA operator display. The 07/08/2025 confirmation is evidence for the record, not a substitute for the §5 confirmation at issuance. This confirmation can be completed at issuance on 08/04/2025.
[24] Normal: C-3. First parallel operation.
[25] Normal: ISA Article 6.3 and DPS-07 §6.3 require the first parallel operation after PTO to be observed by the SOC with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision. This is an operating step after PTO; it does not bar issuance and does not need to be completed before 08/04/2025, but it must be scheduled and recorded by the SOC.
[26] Heading 1: 5. Items reviewed and found acceptable
[27] Normal: Other ISA terms. ISA Article 11.3 requires the Interconnection Customer to maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and to provide a certificate of that insurance on the Company's request. No certificate is in the file and no request is recorded; this is not a PTO condition and I have not treated it as a hold. If a certificate has been requested, it should be obtained before issuance.
[28] Heading 1: 6. Scope and exclusions
[29] Normal: This memo does not review or decide the four matters under separate review: (1) the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser at the site (SCADA/EMS Engineering and Distribution Protection Engineering); (2) the POI recloser's settings and the protection coordination study behind them (Distribution Protection Engineering, which issued them and keeps them outside these records); (3) the site's queue position (Meera Vellanki, under the weekly queue reports); and (4) the system impact study and its conditions (Ivo Grantham's DER Planning Group, which keeps them outside these records). Nothing else is excluded.
[30] Normal: The checklist's statements that the RTU/POI recloser tests were accepted, that the POI recloser settings and coordination study were issued, and that the site is in commissioning are noted for context only. They are not a determination by this memo, and I have not re-reviewed the underlying tests, settings or study.
[31] Heading 1: 7. Recommendation and next steps
[32] List Number: Hold PTO for 08/04/2025. Do not issue PTO on the record as it stands.
[33] List Number: Issue the Office's written notice to Corwyn Realty Partners (attention Nadia Ferreira-Holt) and Brantley Electric Company on 07/15/2025, stating F-1 and the 08/01/2025 deadline for the corrected design, breaker and AHJ re-approval.
[34] List Number: Corwyn/Brantley to complete F-1(a), F-1(b) or F-1(c) and deliver the revised equipment schedule, breaker rating or written code basis, and City of Wrenford re-inspection/final approval to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025.
[35] List Number: Evan Solberg, Standards Engineering, to confirm the CEL-2025-Q3 listing of VX-140C by 08/01/2025 (C-1).
[36] List Number: Lena Kovalchuk/SOC to re-confirm live telemetry at the moment of issuance on 08/04/2025 (C-2), and to schedule the first parallel operation observation under ISA Article 6.3 (C-3).
[37] List Number: If F-1 is closed and C-1 and C-2 are confirmed, the Office may issue PTO on 08/04/2025. If F-1 is not closed, PTO remains on hold and the Office will re-determine when the corrected record is complete. The witness test remains valid; no re-test of the inverter protective functions is required for the main-breaker change.
[38] Normal: Record. This determination and the action items above are recorded in OpenProject work package 47 in the DER Program Backlog Review project.

- **Owner:** Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) through Brantley Electric Company (contractor, permit WEP-25-0317).
- **Action:** (a) replace the SWBD-PV main with a standard 1,000 A breaker (1,000/902 = 111%); or (b) provide a signed supervised-transformer basis accepted by the City of Wrenford; or (c) provide the written next-higher-standard code basis accepted by the City of Wrenford. **DER Program Office action:** issue the written notice to Corwyn Realty Partners (attention Nadia Ferreira-Holt) and Brantley Electric Company on 07/15/2025, stating F-1 (AC conductors) and F-2 (T-1 secondary main) and the 08/01/2025 deadline.

**Pre-PTO confirmation C-1 — CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025.** VX-140C is on CEL-2025-Q2 row 18; CEL-2025-Q3 is planned 07/31/2025. Owner: Evan Solberg, Standards Engineering. Confirm in writing by 08/01/2025 that VX-140C remains listed on the CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025. If delisted, PTO must be held and re-determined.

**Pre-PTO confirmation C-2 — live telemetry at the moment of PTO.** TCS-02 §5 requires the SOC Shift Supervisor's confirmation at issuance. Owner: Lena Kovalchuk/SOC. The 07/08/2025 confirmation is evidence only; re-confirm all required points valid at the SCADA operator display on 08/04/2025.

**Pre-PTO confirmation C-3 — first parallel operation.** ISA Art. 6.3 / DPS-07 §6.3: SOC to observe and record the first parallel operation with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision after PTO.

**Reviewed and acceptable:** ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex executed 09/12/2024 (700 kW ac, feeder ALN-072); witness test WT-0629-01 dated 07/08/2025 all points pass (anti-islanding 0.39–0.46 s vs 2.0 s limit; enter service 301–304 s vs 300 s minimum); CEL-2025-Q2 VX-140C row 18 and certificate VX-CC-25-0522; AHJ final approval WEP-25-0317 dated 07/02/2025; revenue meter RM-0629 set/tested 07/08/2025; DC output and string circuits pass the 40 °C/75 °C check; no Corwyn entry on the 07/14/2025 SOC PTO-Hold Log, hold lists or WO payment ledger.

**Out of scope / separate review:** installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser (SCADA/EMS and Distribution Protection Engineering); POI recloser settings and protection coordination study (Distribution Protection Engineering); queue position (Meera Vellanki); system impact study and conditions (Ivo Grantham/DER Planning Group). [4] 2. Basis: the ISA conditions and the record at 07/14/2025

[5] ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, Article 6.2, permits parallel operation only once four conditions are met: (i) the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted; (ii) telemetry is live at the System Operations Center; (iii) the witness test is complete; and (iv) the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities. Article 4.1 also requires the Facility to conform to DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's Certified Equipment List, each as in effect from time to time. The facility is a 700 kW ac commercial small-scale DER (500 kW–1 MW), DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 Category 2; DPS-07 §4.2 separately requires the utility-owned POI recloser, which the checklist records as installed and accepted. The executed ISA and APUC Tariff §12.6 require the Company's written PTO before parallel operation. I checked each condition against the record as of 07/14/2025.

[6] The four matters placed under separate review are not decided here: (1) the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser; (2) the POI recloser settings and the protection coordination study; (3) the site's queue position; and (4) the system impact study and its conditions. The checklist's entries for (1) and (2) are recorded as complete/accepted/issued on 07/08/2025 and 06/18/2025; I have not re-reviewed the underlying tests, settings or study. Nothing else is outside this memo.

[7] 3. What stands in the way: F-1 — AC inverter output conductor ampacity; F-2 — SWBD-PV main breaker

[8] F-1. The AC inverter output conductors are not verified at the 40 °C design ambient.

[9] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023, Articles 690.8(A)(1) and (B), require the inverter output conductors to carry 125% of the inverter continuous output current (1.25 × 168 A = 210 A) and to be protected by the 225 A breaker (NEC 240.4). Article 110.14(C) limits the conductor to the lowest connected termination temperature (75 °C), and Article 310.15(B)(1) requires the 40 °C ambient correction. The stricter reading applied here corrects the 75 °C terminal ampacity: 230 A × 0.88 = 202.4 A.

[10] What it rests on. Canopy Cable Schedule E-201 Rev C (06/24/2025), rows AC-C1 to AC-C5: 3 × 1/C 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2 plus 1/C 4 AWG Cu ground, 225 A breaker at SWBD-PV, inverter output 168 A; the schedule columns are "Ampacity at 40 °C, 90 °C column 236.6 A" and "Terminal rating 75 °C 230 A"; lengths are 96 to 160 m and voltage drop 1.16% to 1.93%.

[11] Calculation. 4/0 Cu 75 °C ampacity is 230 A; the 40 °C correction is 0.88, giving 202.4 A. That is below the 225 A breaker and below the 210 A required by 690.8. Utilisation is 225/202.4 = 1.112 against the breaker and 210/202.4 = 1.038 against the 690.8 minimum. On the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) reading, the ampacity is 230 A and the conductors would pass; the record does not state which basis the AHJ accepted.

[12] What to do. Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must either (a) upsize the five AC inverter output circuits to a conductor whose 75 °C ampacity corrected for 40 °C is at least 225 A (300 kcmil Cu gives 285 × 0.88 = 250.8 A; 250 kcmil gives 255 × 0.88 = 224.4 A and is not enough), with terminations, conduit, voltage drop and the equipment grounding conductor adjusted per NEC 250.122(B), and obtain AHJ re-inspection and final approval; or (b) provide the City of Wrenford's written acceptance of the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) basis (230 A) and update the record. The 225 A breaker cannot be reduced to 200 A because 690.8 requires at least 210 A.

[13] Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor) for the design, conductors, terminations and AHJ submission; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for re-inspection and final approval; the DER Program Office for verification.

[14] Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Not on the record. The five circuits are installed in 2-1/2 in. rigid metal conduit on the canopy/column and 2-1/2 in. Schedule 40 PVC underground; conductor replacement, termination changes and AHJ re-inspection are not on the record or booked. A written AHJ acceptance of the alternative basis may be achievable, but the record does not contain it. To keep 08/04/2025, Corwyn must complete (a) or (b) and deliver the AHJ acceptance to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025. Otherwise PTO should be held and re-determined when the corrected record is complete.

[15] F-2. The SWBD-PV main breaker is not verified against the T-1 secondary overcurrent-protection limit.

[16] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023, Table 450.3(A) (adopted by the City of Wrenford by Ordinance 24-118 and made part of permit WEP-25-0317), limits the secondary overcurrent device for a transformer over 1,000 V to 125% of the transformer secondary full-load current; the 250% column applies only where the transformer is supervised. ISA Article 4.1 requires the Facility to conform to the Company standards and the code in effect, and ISA Article 6.2 requires the AHJ's final approval of the customer's facilities.

[17] What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, dated 06/24/2025: the T-1 row states 750 kVA, 13.2 kV to 480Y/277 V and a full-load secondary current of 902 A; the SWBD-PV row states a 1,200 A bus and a 1,200 A main breaker. The calculation is 902 A × 1.25 = 1,127.6 A. The installed 1,200 A main is 133% of 902 A and 72.4 A (6.4%) above the 125% value. The record has no supervised-transformer designation, no signed supervision basis, no written next-higher-standard basis, and no AHJ finding specifically addressing the 125%/next-higher basis. The T-1 secondary cable bus rating is also not stated in the record. The 07/02/2025 Certificate of Final Approval records the inspection result but does not document these checks.

[18] Conclusion. On the strict, non-supervised reading of Table 450.3(A) — the reading I apply because the record does not establish supervision — the 1,200 A main exceeds the 125% secondary limit. I therefore cannot verify the T-1 secondary protection as designed. This is a hold item, not a documentation comment. If Corwyn contends that the next-higher standard rating is permitted, it must put the code basis and the AHJ's written acceptance on the record; the record as it stands does not contain either.

[19] What has to be done. Corwyn Realty Partners, through its contractor Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must do one of the following:

[20] (a) Replace the SWBD-PV main breaker with a standard 1,000 A breaker (1,000 A / 902 A = 111%, within 125%), update the equipment schedule and the arc-flash label, and obtain re-inspection and final approval from the City of Wrenford; or

[21] (b) Provide a signed supervised-transformer basis acceptable to the City of Wrenford under Table 450.3(A), with the AHJ's written acceptance, and update the record accordingly; or

[22] (c) Provide the written code basis, and the City of Wrenford's written acceptance, for using the next-higher standard rating under Table 450.3(A) (1,200 A is the next standard rating above 1,127.6 A), and update the record accordingly. The record as it stands contains none of (a), (b) or (c).

[23] The replacement breaker must be rated for the 15.7 kA available fault current and the 35 kA switchboard rating, and the busbar check must remain satisfied: five 225 A inverter breakers plus the 40 A TX-1 breaker = 1,165 A, which is within the 1,200 A bus. The revised equipment schedule must also state the T-1 secondary cable bus rating and show that the 1,000 A (or documented 1,200 A) main protects it.

[24] Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor) for the design, breaker, cable-bus rating, code basis and AHJ submission; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for re-inspection and final approval; the DER Program Office for verification. Distribution Protection Engineering's POI settings and coordination study remain outside this memo; the DER Program Office will notify DPE of the corrected customer-side record for information only.

[25] Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Not on the record.
