[1] 1. Determination

[2] Permission to Operate cannot issue for Corwyn Office Complex PV on 08/04/2025 on the record before me. Three customer-side items are not verified. First, the five AC inverter output circuits use 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2 conductors on 225 A breakers; at the 40 °C design ambient the schedule gives 236.6 A in the 90 °C column and a 75 °C terminal rating of 230 A. On the stricter reading of NEC 110.14(C)/310.15(B)(1), the 75 °C terminal ampacity corrected for 40 °C is 230 × 0.88 = 202.4 A, below both the 225 A breaker and the 210 A required by NEC 690.8 (125% × 168 A). The record does not state that the AHJ accepted the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) basis of 230 A; on that alternative the conductors would pass. Second, the SWBD-PV main breaker is 1,200 A on a 750 kVA transformer whose 480 V secondary full-load current is 902 A (133%); the strict Table 450.3(A) 125% limit is 1,127.6 A, and no supervised or written next-higher-standard basis is on the record. Third, the PV labeling record does not show the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment or the full dc power source label content required by NEC 690.12 and 690.53. The City of Wrenford's final approval of 07/02/2025 and the completed witness test do not cure these items.

[3] The witness test, inverter certification and telemetry record are otherwise in order for the inverter protective functions. Both F-1 and F-2 must be closed, or their AHJ basis documented, before the facility is energized. A separate pre-issuance check of the Certified Equipment List edition in force on 08/04/2025 (CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025) is also required; it is not a present non-conformance but it must be closed before issuance.

[4] 2. Basis: the ISA conditions and the record at 07/14/2025

[5] ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, Article 6.2, permits parallel operation only once four conditions are met: (i) the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted; (ii) telemetry is live at the System Operations Center; (iii) the witness test is complete; and (iv) the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities. Article 4.1 also requires the Facility to conform to DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's Certified Equipment List, each as in effect from time to time. The facility is a 700 kW ac commercial small-scale DER (500 kW–1 MW), DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 Category 2; DPS-07 §4.2 separately requires the utility-owned POI recloser, which the checklist records as installed and accepted. The executed ISA and APUC Tariff §12.6 require the Company's written PTO before parallel operation. I checked each condition against the record as of 07/14/2025.

[6] The four matters placed under separate review are not decided here: (1) the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser; (2) the POI recloser settings and the protection coordination study; (3) the site's queue position; and (4) the system impact study and its conditions. The checklist's entries for (1) and (2) are recorded as complete/accepted/issued on 07/08/2025 and 06/18/2025; I have not re-reviewed the underlying tests, settings or study. Nothing else is outside this memo.

[7] 3. What stands in the way: F-1 — AC inverter output conductor ampacity; F-2 — SWBD-PV main breaker; F-3 — PV labeling

[8] F-1. The AC inverter output conductors are not verified at the 40 °C design ambient.

[9] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023, Sections 690.8(A)(1) and 690.8(B), require the inverter output conductors to carry 125% of the inverter continuous output current (1.25 × 168 A = 210 A) and to be protected by the 225 A breaker (NEC 240.4). Section 110.14(C) limits the conductor to the lowest connected termination temperature (75 °C), and Section 310.15(B)(1) requires the 40 °C ambient correction. The stricter reading applied here corrects the 75 °C terminal ampacity: 230 A × 0.88 = 202.4 A.

[10] What it rests on. Canopy Cable Schedule E-201 Rev C (06/24/2025), rows AC-C1 to AC-C5: 3 × 1/C 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2 plus 1/C 4 AWG Cu ground, 225 A breaker at SWBD-PV, inverter output 168 A; the schedule columns are "Ampacity at 40 °C, 90 °C column 236.6 A" and "Terminal rating 75 °C 230 A"; lengths are 96 to 160 m and voltage drop 1.16% to 1.93%.

[11] Calculation. 4/0 Cu 75 °C ampacity is 230 A; the 40 °C correction is 0.88, giving 202.4 A. That is below the 225 A breaker and below the 210 A required by 690.8. Utilisation is 225/202.4 = 1.112 against the breaker and 210/202.4 = 1.038 against the 690.8 minimum. On the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) reading, the ampacity is 230 A and the conductors would pass; the record does not state which basis the AHJ accepted.

[12] What to do. Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must either (a) upsize the five AC inverter output circuits to a conductor whose 75 °C ampacity corrected for 40 °C is at least 225 A (300 kcmil Cu gives 285 × 0.88 = 250.8 A; 250 kcmil gives 255 × 0.88 = 224.4 A and is not enough), with terminations, conduit, voltage drop and the equipment grounding conductor adjusted per NEC 250.122(B), and obtain AHJ re-inspection and final approval; or (b) provide the City of Wrenford's written acceptance of the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) basis (230 A) and update the record. The 225 A breaker cannot be reduced to 200 A because 690.8 requires at least 210 A.

[13] Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor) for the design, conductors, terminations and AHJ submission; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for re-inspection and final approval; the DER Program Office for verification.

[14] Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Not on the record. The five circuits are installed in 2-1/2 in. rigid metal conduit on the canopy/column and 2-1/2 in. Schedule 40 PVC underground; conductor replacement, termination changes and AHJ re-inspection are not on the record or booked. A written AHJ acceptance of the alternative basis may be achievable, but the record does not contain it. To keep 08/04/2025, Corwyn must complete (a) or (b) and deliver the AHJ acceptance to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025. Otherwise PTO should be held and re-determined when the corrected record is complete.

[15] F-2. The SWBD-PV main breaker is not verified against the T-1 secondary overcurrent-protection limit.

[16] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023, Table 450.3(A) (adopted by the City of Wrenford by Ordinance 24-118 and made part of permit WEP-25-0317), limits the secondary overcurrent device for a transformer over 1,000 V to 125% of the transformer secondary full-load current; the 250% column applies only where the transformer is supervised. ISA Article 4.1 requires the Facility to conform to the Company standards and the code in effect, and ISA Article 6.2 requires the AHJ's final approval of the customer's facilities.

[17] What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, dated 06/24/2025: the T-1 row states 750 kVA, 13.2 kV to 480Y/277 V and a full-load secondary current of 902 A; the SWBD-PV row states a 1,200 A bus and a 1,200 A main breaker. The calculation is 902 A × 1.25 = 1,127.6 A. The installed 1,200 A main is 133% of 902 A and 72.4 A (6.4%) above the 125% value. The record has no supervised-transformer designation, no signed supervision basis, no written next-higher-standard basis, and no AHJ finding specifically addressing the 125%/next-higher basis. The T-1 secondary cable bus rating is also not stated in the record. The 07/02/2025 Certificate of Final Approval records the inspection result but does not document these checks.

[18] Conclusion. On the strict, non-supervised reading of Table 450.3(A) — the reading I apply because the record does not establish supervision — the 1,200 A main exceeds the 125% secondary limit. I therefore cannot verify the T-1 secondary protection as designed. This is a hold item, not a documentation comment. If Corwyn contends that the next-higher standard rating is permitted, it must put the code basis and the AHJ's written acceptance on the record; the record as it stands does not contain either.

[19] What has to be done. Corwyn Realty Partners, through its contractor Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must do one of the following:

[20] (a) Replace the SWBD-PV main breaker with a standard 1,000 A breaker (1,000 A / 902 A = 111%, within 125%), update the equipment schedule and the arc-flash label, and obtain re-inspection and final approval from the City of Wrenford; or

[21] (b) Provide a signed supervised-transformer basis acceptable to the City of Wrenford under Table 450.3(A), with the AHJ's written acceptance, and update the record accordingly; or

[22] (c) Provide the written code basis, and the City of Wrenford's written acceptance, for using the next-higher standard rating under Table 450.3(A) (1,200 A is the next standard rating above 1,127.6 A), and update the record accordingly. The record as it stands contains none of (a), (b) or (c).

[23] The replacement breaker must be rated for the 15.7 kA available fault current and the 35 kA switchboard rating, and the busbar check must remain satisfied: five 225 A inverter breakers plus the 40 A TX-1 breaker = 1,165 A, which is within the 1,200 A bus. The revised equipment schedule must also state the T-1 secondary cable bus rating and show that the 1,000 A (or documented 1,200 A) main protects it.

[24] Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor) for the design, breaker, cable-bus rating, code basis and AHJ submission; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for re-inspection and final approval; the DER Program Office for verification. Distribution Protection Engineering's POI settings and coordination study remain outside this memo; the DER Program Office will notify DPE of the corrected customer-side record for information only.

[25] Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Not on the record. As of 07/14/2025 there is no revised drawing, no breaker order or availability confirmation, no signed supervision/next-higher basis, no T-1 secondary cable-bus rating, and no AHJ re-inspection booked; the 07/02/2025 final approval is for the 1,200 A design. A 1,000 A breaker and a re-inspection, or a written code/AHJ basis, may be achievable in the time available, but the record does not demonstrate it. To keep 08/04/2025, Corwyn must complete (a), (b) or (c) and deliver the AHJ acceptance to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025. Otherwise PTO should be held and re-determined when the corrected record is complete. The witness test remains valid; the corrections do not require re-testing the inverter protective functions.

[26] F-3. The PV labeling record is incomplete.

[27] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023 Section 690.12(B)(2)(3) requires a permanent plaque at the service equipment identifying the rapid shutdown system and its initiator; Section 690.53 requires the dc power source label to provide the maximum voltage, maximum current, maximum rated output current and maximum rated output power of the dc source. The permit adopts NFPA 70-2023.

[28] What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, Labels row: arc-flash labels, the SWBD-PV voltage/fault-current/clearing-time label, source-location plaques at SWBD-PV and PSW-1, the AD-C inverter-disconnect labels, the SWBD-PV main PV-system-disconnect label, and dc power source labels "giving the maximum dc voltage, 958.6 V." The row does not record a rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment, and the dc labels do not record maximum current or rated output current. String Schedule E-301 records module-level rapid shutdown devices and the initiator at the SWBD-PV main, but no service-equipment plaque.

[29] Conclusion. The record does not demonstrate the required rapid shutdown plaque or the full dc label content. This is a labeling non-conformance; it can be corrected without changing the electrical design.

[30] What to do. Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must install the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment identifying the system and initiator, complete the dc power source labels with the values required by Section 690.53, and provide a photographed as-built label record. The City of Wrenford is to confirm the labels at re-inspection.

[31] Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners and Brantley Electric Company for the labels; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for inspection; the DER Program Office for verification.

[32] Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Yes — this is a labeling correction and does not require conductor or breaker changes. It can be completed and inspected before 08/04/2025 if scheduled. It remains a hold until the as-built label record is on file. To keep 08/04/2025, deliver the label record and AHJ confirmation to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025.

[33] 4. Pre-issuance confirmations (to be closed before PTO, not present non-conformances)

[34] C-1. CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025.

[35] ISA Article 4.1 requires conformity with the Certified Equipment List as in effect from time to time. CEL-2025-Q2 (04/30/2025) lists VX-140C at row 18 and is the edition checked on the 07/14/2025 checklist. CEL-2025-Q2 states that CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025, before the requested PTO date. Evan Solberg, Standards Engineering, is to confirm in writing by 08/01/2025 that VX-140C remains listed on the CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025. If it is delisted, the facility cannot be verified against the current CEL and PTO must be held and re-determined; if it remains listed, this condition is closed. This confirmation can be completed by 08/01/2025.

[36] C-2. Live telemetry at the moment of PTO.

[37] TCS-02 §5 and ISA Articles 6.2 and 7.2 require live telemetry at the SOC when PTO is issued, with the SOC Shift Supervisor's confirmation recorded against the file. The checklist records the 07/08/2025 confirmation by L. Kovalchuk, and the 07/14/2025 SOC PTO-Hold Log has no Corwyn entry. Lena Kovalchuk/SOC is to re-confirm at the moment of issuance on 08/04/2025 that all required points are valid (not stale, forced or bad-quality) at the SCADA operator display. The 07/08/2025 confirmation is evidence for the record, not a substitute for the §5 confirmation at issuance. This confirmation can be completed at issuance on 08/04/2025.

[38] C-3. First parallel operation.

[39] ISA Article 6.3 and DPS-07 §6.3 require the first parallel operation after PTO to be observed by the SOC with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision. This is an operating step after PTO; it does not bar issuance and does not need to be completed before 08/04/2025, but it must be scheduled and recorded by the SOC.

[40] 5. Items reviewed and found acceptable

[41] Other ISA terms. ISA Article 11.3 requires the Interconnection Customer to maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and to provide a certificate of that insurance on the Company's request. No certificate is in the file and no request is recorded; this is not a PTO condition and I have not treated it as a hold. If a certificate has been requested, it should be obtained before issuance.

[42] 6. Scope and exclusions

[43] This memo does not review or decide the four matters under separate review: (1) the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser at the site (SCADA/EMS Engineering and Distribution Protection Engineering); (2) the POI recloser's settings and the protection coordination study behind them (Distribution Protection Engineering, which issued them and keeps them outside these records); (3) the site's queue position (Meera Vellanki, under the weekly queue reports); and (4) the system impact study and its conditions (Ivo Grantham's DER Planning Group, which keeps them outside these records). Nothing else is excluded.

[44] The checklist's statements that the RTU/POI recloser tests were accepted, that the POI recloser settings and coordination study were issued, and that the site is in commissioning are noted for context only. **Pre-PTO confirmation C-1 — CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025.** VX-140C is on CEL-2025-Q2 row 18; CEL-2025-Q3 is planned 07/31/2025. Owner: Evan Solberg, Standards Engineering. [0][Normal] 
[1][Heading 1] 1. Determination
[2][Normal] Permission to Operate cannot issue for Corwyn Office Complex PV on 08/04/2025 on the record before me. Three customer-side items are not verified. First, the five AC inverter output circuits use 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2 conductors on 225 A breakers; at the 40 °C design ambient the schedule gives 236.6 A in the 90 °C column and a 75 °C terminal rating of 230 A. On the stricter reading of NEC 110.14(C)/310.15(B)(1), the 75 °C terminal ampacity corrected for 40 °C is 230 × 0.88 = 202.4 A, below both the 225 A breaker and the 210 A required by NEC 690.8 (125% × 168 A). The record does not state that the AHJ accepted the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) basis of 230 A; on that alternative the conductors would pass. Second, the SWBD-PV main breaker is 1,200 A on a 750 kVA transformer whose 480 V secondary full-load current is 902 A (133%); the strict Table 450.3(A) 125% limit is 1,127.6 A, and no supervised or written next-higher-standard basis is on the record. Third, the PV labeling record does not show the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment or the full dc power source label content required by NEC 690.12 and 690.53. The City of Wrenford's final approval of 07/02/2025 and the completed witness test do not cure these items.
[3][Normal] The witness test, inverter certification and telemetry record are otherwise in order for the inverter protective functions. F-1, F-2 and F-3 must be closed, or their AHJ basis documented, before the facility is energized. A separate pre-issuance check of the Certified Equipment List edition in force on 08/04/2025 (CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025) is also required; it is not a present non-conformance but it must be closed before issuance.
[4][Heading 1] 2. Basis: the ISA conditions and the record at 07/14/2025
[5][Normal] ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, Article 6.2, permits parallel operation only once four conditions are met: (i) the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted; (ii) telemetry is live at the System Operations Center; (iii) the witness test is complete; and (iv) the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities. Article 4.1 also requires the Facility to conform to DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's Certified Equipment List, each as in effect from time to time. The facility is a 700 kW ac commercial small-scale DER (500 kW–1 MW), DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 Category 2; DPS-07 §4.2 separately requires the utility-owned POI recloser, which the checklist records as installed and accepted. The executed ISA and APUC Tariff §12.6 require the Company's written PTO before parallel operation. I checked each condition against the record as of 07/14/2025.
[6][Normal] The four matters placed under separate review are not decided here: (1) the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser; (2) the POI recloser settings and the protection coordination study; (3) the site's queue position; and (4) the system impact study and its conditions. The checklist's entries for (1) and (2) are recorded as complete/accepted/issued on 07/08/2025 and 06/18/2025; I have not re-reviewed the underlying tests, settings or study. Nothing else is outside this memo.
[7][Heading 1] 3. What stands in the way: F-1 — AC inverter output conductor ampacity; F-2 — SWBD-PV main breaker; F-3 — PV labeling
[8][Normal] F-1. The AC inverter output conductors are not verified at the 40 °C design ambient.
[9][Normal] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023, Sections 690.8(A)(1) and 690.8(B), require the inverter output conductors to carry 125% of the inverter continuous output current (1.25 × 168 A = 210 A) and to be protected by the 225 A breaker (NEC 240.4). Section 110.14(C) limits the conductor to the lowest connected termination temperature (75 °C), and Section 310.15(B)(1) requires the 40 °C ambient correction. The stricter reading applied here corrects the 75 °C terminal ampacity: 230 A × 0.88 = 202.4 A.
[10][Normal] What it rests on. Canopy Cable Schedule E-201 Rev C (06/24/2025), rows AC-C1 to AC-C5: 3 × 1/C 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2 plus 1/C 4 AWG Cu ground, 225 A breaker at SWBD-PV, inverter output 168 A; the schedule columns are "Ampacity at 40 °C, 90 °C column 236.6 A" and "Terminal rating 75 °C 230 A"; lengths are 96 to 160 m and voltage drop 1.16% to 1.93%.
[11][Normal] Calculation. 4/0 Cu 75 °C ampacity is 230 A; the 40 °C correction is 0.88, giving 202.4 A. That is below the 225 A breaker and below the 210 A required by 690.8. Utilisation is 225/202.4 = 1.112 against the breaker and 210/202.4 = 1.038 against the 690.8 minimum. On the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) reading, the ampacity is 230 A and the conductors would pass; the record does not state which basis the AHJ accepted.
[12][Normal] What to do. Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must either (a) upsize the five AC inverter output circuits to a conductor whose 75 °C ampacity corrected for 40 °C is at least 225 A (300 kcmil Cu gives 285 × 0.88 = 250.8 A; 250 kcmil gives 255 × 0.88 = 224.4 A and is not enough), with terminations, conduit, voltage drop and the equipment grounding conductor adjusted per NEC 250.122(B), and obtain AHJ re-inspection and final approval; or (b) provide the City of Wrenford's written acceptance of the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) basis (230 A) and update the record. The 225 A breaker cannot be reduced to 200 A because 690.8 requires at least 210 A.
[13][Normal] Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor) for the design, conductors, terminations and AHJ submission; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for re-inspection and final approval; the DER Program Office for verification.
[14][Normal] Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Not on the record. The five circuits are installed in 2-1/2 in. rigid metal conduit on the canopy/column and 2-1/2 in. Schedule 40 PVC underground; conductor replacement, termination changes and AHJ re-inspection are not on the record or booked. A written AHJ acceptance of the alternative basis may be achievable, but the record does not contain it. To keep 08/04/2025, Corwyn must complete (a) or (b) and deliver the AHJ acceptance to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025. Otherwise PTO should be held and re-determined when the corrected record is complete.
[15][Normal] F-2. The SWBD-PV main breaker is not verified against the T-1 secondary overcurrent-protection limit.
[16][Normal] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023, Table 450.3(A) (adopted by the City of Wrenford by Ordinance 24-118 and made part of permit WEP-25-0317), limits the secondary overcurrent device for a transformer over 1,000 V to 125% of the transformer secondary full-load current; the 250% column applies only where the transformer is supervised. ISA Article 4.1 requires the Facility to conform to the Company standards and the code in effect, and ISA Article 6.2 requires the AHJ's final approval of the customer's facilities.
[17][Normal] What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, dated 06/24/2025: the T-1 row states 750 kVA, 13.2 kV to 480Y/277 V and a full-load secondary current of 902 A; the SWBD-PV row states a 1,200 A bus and a 1,200 A main breaker. The calculation is 902 A × 1.25 = 1,127.6 A. The installed 1,200 A main is 133% of 902 A and 72.4 A (6.4%) above the 125% value. The record has no supervised-transformer designation, no signed supervision basis, no written next-higher-standard basis, and no AHJ finding specifically addressing the 125%/next-higher basis. The T-1 secondary cable bus rating is also not stated in the record. The 07/02/2025 Certificate of Final Approval records the inspection result but does not document these checks.
[18][Normal] Conclusion. On the strict, non-supervised reading of Table 450.3(A) — the reading I apply because the record does not establish supervision — the 1,200 A main exceeds the 125% secondary limit. I therefore cannot verify the T-1 secondary protection as designed. This is a hold item, not a documentation comment. If Corwyn contends that the next-higher standard rating is permitted, it must put the code basis and the AHJ's written acceptance on the record; the record as it stands does not contain either.
[19][Normal] What has to be done. Corwyn Realty Partners, through its contractor Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must do one of the following:
[20][List Bullet] (a) Replace the SWBD-PV main breaker with a standard 1,000 A breaker (1,000 A / 902 A = 111%, within 125%), update the equipment schedule and the arc-flash label, and obtain re-inspection and final approval from the City of Wrenford; or
[21][List Bullet] (b) Provide a signed supervised-transformer basis acceptable to the City of Wrenford under Table 450.3(A), with the AHJ's written acceptance, and update the record accordingly; or
[22][List Bullet] (c) Provide the written code basis, and the City of Wrenford's written acceptance, for using the next-higher standard rating under Table 450.3(A) (1,200 A is the next standard rating above 1,127.6 A), and update the record accordingly. The record as it stands contains none of (a), (b) or (c).
[23][Normal] The replacement breaker must be rated for the 15.7 kA available fault current and the 35 kA switchboard rating, and the busbar check must remain satisfied: five 225 A inverter breakers plus the 40 A TX-1 breaker = 1,165 A, which is within the 1,200 A bus. The revised equipment schedule must also state the T-1 secondary cable bus rating and show that the 1,000 A (or documented 1,200 A) main protects it.
[24][Normal] Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor) for the design, breaker, cable-bus rating, code basis and AHJ submission; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for re-inspection and final approval; the DER Program Office for verification. Distribution Protection Engineering's POI settings and coordination study remain outside this memo; the DER Program Office will notify DPE of the corrected customer-side record for information only.
[25][Normal] Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Not on the record. As of 07/14/2025 there is no revised drawing, no breaker order or availability confirmation, no signed supervision/next-higher basis, no T-1 secondary cable-bus rating, and no AHJ re-inspection booked; the 07/02/2025 final approval is for the 1,200 A design. A 1,000 A breaker and a re-inspection, or a written code/AHJ basis, may be achievable in the time available, but the record does not demonstrate it. To keep 08/04/2025, Corwyn must complete (a), (b) or (c) and deliver the AHJ acceptance to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025. Otherwise PTO should be held and re-determined when the corrected record is complete. The witness test remains valid; the corrections do not require re-testing the inverter protective functions.
[26][Normal] F-3. The PV labeling record is incomplete.
[27][Normal] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023 Section 690.12(B)(2)(3) requires a permanent plaque at the service equipment identifying the rapid shutdown system and its initiator; Section 690.53 requires the dc power source label to provide the maximum voltage, maximum current, maximum rated output current and maximum rated output power of the dc source. The permit adopts NFPA 70-2023.
[28][Normal] What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, Labels row: arc-flash labels, the SWBD-PV voltage/fault-current/clearing-time label, source-location plaques at SWBD-PV and PSW-1, the AD-C inverter-disconnect labels, the SWBD-PV main PV-system-disconnect label, and dc power source labels "giving the maximum dc voltage, 958.6 V." The row does not record a rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment, and the dc labels do not record maximum current or rated output current. String Schedule E-301 records module-level rapid shutdown devices and the initiator at the SWBD-PV main, but no service-equipment plaque.
[29][Normal] Conclusion. The record does not demonstrate the required rapid shutdown plaque or the full dc label content. This is a labeling non-conformance; it can be corrected without changing the electrical design.
[30][Normal] What to do. Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must install the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment identifying the system and initiator, complete the dc power source labels with the values required by Section 690.53, and provide a photographed as-built label record. The City of Wrenford is to confirm the labels at re-inspection.

§1 Purpose and Scope
This standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy
resources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state
interconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes
defined in §3.
DIS-01 Rev 4 governs:
• classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);
• eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
• recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);
• protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);

• treatment of post-execution changes to executed interconnection service agreements (§7).
This standard is read together with the APUC-filed interconnection tariff (§12). Where a topic is addressed by both
this standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration
are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.
§2 References
The following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision
applies.
• IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources
with Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
• DPS-07 Rev 2 — Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023). Establishes distribution
protection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope
facilities.
• TCS-02 — Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021). Governs utility-owned RTU
installation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition
for permission to operate.
• CEL-2025-Q2 — Alleniom Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025). Listing basis: UL 1741-SB and UL
3141. The CEL front matter restates §3.6 of this standard.
• ERP-9 — Alleniom Engineering Referral Procedure (Form ER-11). §3 routes any standards 
§3 DER Classification
DER facilities are classified by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling, in accordance with
IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.
Commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER
(commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.
Definitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the
APUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings
assigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),
export-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility
interconnection practice.

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.
§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.
§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.
§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.
§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.
§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.


--- page 4 ---
DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard
Page 4
DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024
The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
1.  Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
2.  Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.
§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.
Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
1.  A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
setpoint range.
2.  An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.
Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:
• Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
• POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
additional utility hardware.
Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.
No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.
Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific
certification and Control Narrative are always required.


--- page 5 ---

DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024

Applications in DER Program scope proceed through initial technical screening under Interconnection Studies.
Facilities not passing initial screens may be evaluated under supplemental review per SRP-3 or advance to a system
impact study. This standard does not restate SRP-3; the daytime minimum-load convention and other screen
methodologies are prescribed there.

2.  Table 5-1 addresses protective and control equipment. Monitoring and communications requirements are
established under TCS-02.
3.  Where §3.6 recognition is in effect at a pure-generation site with a utility POI recloser, the ANSI 32
directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips on violation.
§6 Monitoring and Control
Facilities at or above the TCS-02 program threshold shall provide real-time monitoring and control integration through
a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system
operations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5
for the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.
Site-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection
relay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the
control-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.
§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
permitted for capacity or POI changes.
Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
invoking this section.
Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
executed.
Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
interconnection after ISA execution shall:
1.  Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
2.  File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
3.  Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
applicant as involving new or existing equipment.
Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.
Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.
§8 Records and Compliance
Interconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the
retention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this
standard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral
Procedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.

DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard
Page 7
DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024
Any conflict between this standard and the APUC-filed tariff is resolved in favor of the tariff. Any conflict between this
standard and another Alleniom operating standard encountered in screening or study is referred to per-site
engineering determination under ERP-9 §3.
End of DIS-01 Rev 4.

5.1 Company's Facilities. The Company provides, owns and operates the POI recloser (DPS-07 §4.2), the RTU (TCS-02 §3) and revenue meter RM-0629 with 13.2 kV primary metering at the Point of Interconnection, at the Interconnection Customer's cost under the construction work order.

The Interconnection Customer provides, owns and maintains the interconnection facilities identified in Exhibit B and the site provisions for the Company's Facilities (equipment pad, primary conductors to the recloser terminals, and the station service and communications entrance for the RTU) as specified in the Company's construction package.
5.3 Access. The Interconnection Customer grants the Company access at all times to the Point of Interconnection, the revenue meter and the Facility's disconnects.
ARTICLE 6 — COMMISSIONING AND PERMISSION TO OPERATE
6.1 Witness test. Before permission to operate, the Company may place the Facility in parallel with its distribution system solely for the witness test of the Facility under the Company's Witness Test & Waiver Procedure, under a Distribution Operations switching order and with the System Operations Center observing. At all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open.
6.2 Permission to operate. Parallel operation begins only with the Company's written permission to operate, issued once the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted, telemetry is live at the System Operations Center, the witness test is complete, and the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities.
6.3 First parallel operation. The first parallel operation after permission to operate is observed by the System Operations Center with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision (DPS-07 §6.3).
ARTICLE 7 — METERING AND TELEMETRY
7.1 Metering. Revenue-quality bidirectional metering is provided at the Point of Interconnection, owned, installed, tested and maintained by the Company at the Interconnection Customer's cost, and sealed at all times.
7.2 Telemetry. In accordance with TCS-02 §5, the Interconnection Customer provides, at its cost, the provisions for the Company's RTU and makes available the analog and status points that TCS-02 requires. Live telemetry at the System Operations Center is a condition of permission to operate, and any loss of telemetry after permission to operate is reported and remedied as TCS-02 provides.
ARTICLE 8 — OPERATION
8.1 Operating representatives. The Company's operating representative is the System Operations Center. The Interconnection Customer's operating representative is the Corwyn Office Complex property management office, reachable at all times at (612) 555-0827. Each Party gives the other its operating notices through these representatives.
8.2 Loss of the utility source. On any loss of the utility source at the Point of Interconnection, the Facility shall cease to energize within 2.0 seconds.
8.3 Disconnection by the Company. The Company may open the POI recloser and keep the Facility disconnected for a system emergency, for work on its distribution system, on loss of telemetry, or where the Facility fails to meet this Agreement, with notice to the Interconnection Customer where practicable.
8.4 Reconnection. After the Company has opened the POI recloser, the Facility is placed back in parallel only on the release of the System Operations Center.
8.5 Clearances. On the Company's request the Interconnection Customer opens and padlocks the Facility's disconnects identified in Exhibit B for a clearance and keeps them open until the Company releases the clearance.
8.6 Planned outages. The Interconnection Customer gives the System Operations Center five (5) business days' notice of any planned outage of the Facility longer than one day.
8.7 Changes. The Interconnection Customer makes no change to the Facility's equipment or settings without the Company's written consent under Article 12.
ARTICLE 9 — MAINTENANCE AND RECORDS
9.1 The Interconnection Customer maintains the Facility in accordance with the Standards and the manufacturers' instructions.
9.2 The Interconnection Customer tests the Facility's protective functions on a schedule not longer than that of comparable Company equipment and makes the records available to the Company on request (DPS-07 §6.4).
9.3 The Interconnection Customer keeps operating and maintenance records for the Facility for the term of this Agreement and makes them available to the Company on request.
ARTICLE 10 — PAYMENT
10.1 The Interconnection Customer pays for the Company's Facilities in accordance with the construction work order issued under this Agreement and Tariff §12.5.
10.2 Invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the invoice date. Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the rate set forth in the Tariff.
ARTICLE 11 — LIABILITY AND INSURANCE
11.1 Each Party is responsible for the facilities it owns under this Agreement.
11.2 The Interconnection Customer indemnifies the Company against third-party claims arising from the operation of the Facility, except to the extent caused by the Company's negligence.
11.3 During the term the Interconnection Customer maintains commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and provides a certificate of that insurance on the Company's request.
ARTICLE 12 — AMENDMENTS
12.1 No term of this Agreement may be modified or waived except by an instrument in writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.
12.2 Changes to the capacity or the Point of Interconnection are governed by DIS §7. Other changes to the Facility are made by change order under Section 12.1.

§1   PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.
§2   SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
•
a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
•
b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
•
c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
•
d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common
coupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the
aggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.
§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1   Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.3   Functional requirements
Each RTU shall, at minimum:
•
a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
•
b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
processors over an approved communications path (§4).
•
c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
restoration.
•
d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.
•
e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.
§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5   Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.
§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification
§3.2   Approved models
The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).

Prior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end
point-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,
exercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.
Commissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.
§4   COMMUNICATIONS
§4.1   Communications transport
The RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by
SCADA/EMS Engineering:
•
a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or
•
b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or
•
c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held
by Alleniom.
Customer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.
Where site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for
interconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.
§4.2   SCADA protocol
The RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure
Authentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration
parameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —
shall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§4.3   Availability
The end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a
monthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent
loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be
corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
equipment.
§4.4   Address and IP management
All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate
connections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration
record.
§5   TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE
§5.   ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.
This requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under
DIS-01 §3.4.
Live telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:
•
a.   Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;

Analog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3
Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than
every sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an
integrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be
reported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.
§6.3   Data quality
Every value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,
restart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the
RTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be
reported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.
§6.4   Retention
Alleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six
(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,
engineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.
§7   CYBERSECURITY
§7.1   Applicability
The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.
§7.2   Access control
Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.
§7.3   Communications security
DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.
§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management
RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following
the Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a
cryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or
reconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.
§7.5   Logging and monitoring
The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
procedure.

§7.6   Physical security
The RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any
physical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a
status point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.
§7.7   Incident response
The customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its
enclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and
utility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to
SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§7.8   Decommissioning
At end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.
Customer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided
credentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.
End of TCS-02.

1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
•
IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
•
IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
•
IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
•
ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.


--- page 2 ---

Page 2
•
Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
•
Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
communications shall not defeat local protection.
Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.


--- page 3 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 3
5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
clearance holds.
6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
premises.
4.3 DER-Side Protection
DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.
4.4 Grounding
The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.
4.5 Anti-Islanding
The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.
5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
(a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
recloser.
(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
site's operating procedure.
(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
prior to energization.
5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.
5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.
5.4 Reclosing Blocking
Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the


--- page 4 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 4
affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
5.5 Settings Governance
All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
the field without a written revision order.
6. TESTING
6.1 Factory Acceptance
The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
shipment.
6.2 Site Acceptance
Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
by Alleniom Utilities:
1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
and reset.
4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.
6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.
6.4 Periodic Testing
The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.
6.5 Post-Event Testing
Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.
End of DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard. Distribution: Alleniom Standards Engineering master file;
Distribution Protection Engineering; Distribution Operations; DER Program Office; APUC filing (informational).
Engineering and recorded in the site's interconnection file.

§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.
This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.


--- page 2 ---
§2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:
(1)  Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
the affected site.
(2)  An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
exception).
(3)  The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.
Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).
§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.
The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.
Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.
The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.
Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.
Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.


--- page 3 ---
§4 TIMELINES
Timelines below run from the date on which Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11
to Distribution Protection Engineering. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays.

Classification is made by the Manager, Distribution Protection Engineering, on receipt of Form ER-11.
Where the reviewer requests reclassification, the request is decided in writing within two business days.
Extensions to the timelines above are permitted only in writing, are issued by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and are copied to the DER Program Manager and Regulatory Affairs. Applications
shall not be held in queue pending revision of a standard where this procedure provides a determination
path; extensions do not authorize a screening hold outside this procedure.
§5 DOCUMENTATION
The completed Form ER-11, the engineering determination, and any supporting studies are filed with the
application record retained by Interconnection Studies for the retention period established by Regulatory
Affairs. A copy of the completed Form ER-11 is filed in the Standards Engineering ERP-9 register of
per-site determinations.
The ERP-9 register records, at minimum: the referral number, the receipt date, the Project ID, the site type
and feeder, the standards documents at issue, the assigned engineer, the determination date, and a short
summary of the determination. The register is reviewed by Standards Engineering quarterly for recurring
patterns; where a pattern warrants a standards revision proposal, Standards Engineering initiates that
revision separately from, and in parallel with, ongoing per-site determinations under this procedure. A
pending revision proposal does not stay determinations issued under this procedure and does not
authorize a screening hold on affected applications.
Determinations issued under ERP-9 are cited in the interconnection service agreement (ISA) drafted for
the affected site by reference to the ER-11 referral number and determination date. Modifications to the
site's protection arrangement subsequent to ISA execution are handled under the change-order provisions
of the executed ISA, subject to DIS-01 §7 where capacity or POI is affected.
