ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1.
The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2.
Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3.
Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4.
Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.

--- page 2 ---
ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office
Page 2
5.
The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:
•
the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;
•
for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;


--- page 3 ---
ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office
Page 3
•
for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
date;
•
the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
the CEL listing relied upon;
•
correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
test-plan negotiation.
The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
against the current CEL edition.
End of procedure. See DIS-01 Rev 4 for interconnection standards, TCS-02 for telemetry requirements, and the
current CEL edition for the list of qualifying equipment. Revisions to this procedure are issued by Standards
Engineering and take effect on the date shown in the document-control block above.

§12.1 Applicability
This section governs the interconnection to Alleniom Utilities' (the “Company”) distribution system
of distributed energy resources (“DER”) within the Alleron service territory. Technical
requirements, screens, study procedures, and equipment standards referenced herein are set out
in the Company's DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01) and companion standards, each of
which is incorporated by reference. Nothing in this section shall be construed to modify or
supersede any applicable safety, reliability, or protection requirement of the Company's
engineering standards.

§12.2 Scope of the DER Interconnection Program
The DER Interconnection Program administered under this section applies to applications for DER
interconnection at or above five hundred kilowatts (≥500 kW). Within the Program, DER shall be
classified according to the DER Interconnection Standard as follows:
(a)  Commercial small-scale DER — five hundred kilowatts to one megawatt (500 kW – 1
MW);
(b)  Medium-scale DER — one megawatt to five megawatts (1 MW – 5 MW).
The Program scope threshold is ≥500 kW. DER below five hundred kilowatts (sub-500 kW),
whether commercial or residential, are not administered under this section and shall instead be
processed under the Company's Simplified Small-Systems Process, which is filed separately
and is outside the DER Interconnection Program.
Aggregation, controlled-capacity recognition, and shared point-of-interconnection eligibility are
addressed in the DER Interconnection Standard and shall control the classification of any facility
whose nameplate rating, aggregate site rating, or point of common coupling brings it within
Program scope.

§12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position
A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company
determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be
returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which
cure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly
provided in the DER Interconnection Standard.
§12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation
Upon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the
Company, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit
a substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within
thirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the
active queue without further action of the Company.
For purposes of this section, “business days” shall exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and federal
legal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following
federal holidays falling within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized
as non-business days and shall not be counted:
Holiday

06/19/2025

07/04/2025
The Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall be served in writing (certified mail or
verified electronic delivery) and shall state the date of issuance, the response deadline computed
under this section, and the consequence of non-response. The Company shall maintain a log of all
notices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.

§12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults
Where a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the
customer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of
the outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from
the date of that written notice.
For so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall
remain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment
default procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the
deemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different
consequences, and different cure paths.
Upon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly
release the hold and resume the affected work in queue order. If the deadline expires without
payment, the Company may pursue such remedies as are available under the applicable
Interconnection Service Agreement and this tariff, including, as a separate and subsequent step,
issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §12.4.

§12.6 Interconnection Service Agreement
Interconnection service shall commence only upon execution of an Interconnection Service
Agreement (“ISA”) and the Company's written Permission to Operate. Material terms of an
executed ISA, including but not limited to nameplate facility capacity and the designated point of
interconnection, may not be modified by amendment. Post-execution changes to such material
terms require withdrawal of the affected application and re-application in accordance with the DER
Interconnection Standard.
§12.7 Nondiscriminatory Queue-Order Processing of Applications
Applications shall be processed by the Company in queue order on a nondiscriminatory basis.
No applicant shall be advanced or disadvantaged in the processing sequence by reason of
identity, affiliation, customer class, geography, or any other factor not expressly provided for in this
tariff or in the DER Interconnection Standard.
Scope note. This §12.7 applies to APPLICATION PROCESSING only — that is, to the
sequencing of screening, technical review, study assignment, and issuance of interconnection
determinations. Utility construction sequencing and the scheduling and allocation of constrained
utility-owned

(Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline), which sets forth the criticality factors and
prioritization criteria applicable to constrained equipment. Nothing in this §12.7 shall be construed
to require the Company to sequence construction or equipment deployment in queue order where
OG-17 or another operating guideline provides a different criticality-based ordering.

---
name: electrical-power-design
description: LV/MV power distribution design - load schedules and demand, conductor and device sizing (ampacity, terminal ratings, 125 % rules), voltage drop, short-circuit currents and equipment ratings, transformers, grounding, motor circuits, NEC and IEC 60364 bases. Use for any electrical design or check.
---

# Electrical power distribution design (designer's and checker's practice)
Project documents govern (adopted code edition, spec, utility rules, drawings). Values below are typical or from a recent
NEC edition; section numbers move between editions: cite the adopted one and re-read its table before quoting.

## 0. Order of work and sanity checks
Basis (voltages, grounding, utility fault kA and X/R, code, spec) -> load schedules -> demand -> feeders/transformers ->
conductors (ampacity, then VD) -> fault current per bus -> ratings -> selectivity -> grounding; one script, one size set.
- 3φ I = S/(√3·V_LL) = P/(√3·V_LL·PF); 1φ I = S/V. A per kVA: 480 V 1.203; 400 V 1.443; 208 V 2.776; 240 V 1φ 4.167;
  4.16 kV 0.139; 13.8 kV 0.0418. 1 hp = 0.746 kW (≈ 1 kVA/hp for motors). 1 kcmil = 0.5067 mm²; AWG 10 = 5.26 mm²,
  6 = 13.3, 2 = 33.6, 1/0 = 53.5, 4/0 = 107.2; 500 kcmil = 253 mm². 1 VA/ft² = 10.76 VA/m².

## 1. Load schedule and demand (NEC Art. 220)
- VA per circuit by phase; balance phases. Continuous = max current for ≥ 3 h (office/retail lighting, EVSE, heaters).
- Lighting: occupancy unit load (dwelling 3 VA/ft²; office 1.3 VA/ft² from NEC 2020, 3.5 before) or actual if larger.
  Receptacles 180 VA/yoke, non-dwelling demand first 10 kVA 100 %, rest 50 %. Dwelling: 2 × 1500 VA small appliance +
  1500 VA laundry; lighting 3 kVA at 100 %, to 120 kVA 35 %, rest 25 %; ≥ 4 fixed appliances 75 %; dryer ≥ 5 kVA;
  ranges Table 220.55. Sign outlet 1200 VA; EVSE max(7200 W, nameplate) (NEC 2020+).
- Motors 125 % largest FLC + others (430.24). Noncoincident loads (heat vs cool): larger only. Existing service: 125 % of
  12-month peak 15-min demand (220.87). Neutral: 100 % to 200 A + 70 % above, no reduction for nonlinear loads.
- Demand factor = max demand/connected (≤ 1); diversity factor = Σ individual maxima/coincident max (≥ 1); load factor
  = average/peak. Apply diversity once, where loads actually combine. Add spare capacity per spec (often 20-25 %).

## 2. Conductors and OCPD (NEC 210/215/240/310)
- OCPD ≥ 125 % continuous + 100 % noncontinuous (100 % only for assemblies listed for it). Conductor: (a) table ampacity
  in the terminal-temperature column ≥ 125 % cont + 100 % noncont; (b) ampacity after correction/adjustment ≥ load;
  (c) protected by the OCPD. Terminals (110.14(C)): ≤ 100 A or 14-1 AWG -> 60 °C unless listed 75 °C; > 100 A -> 75 °C;
  90 °C column only as the derating start.
- Table 310.16 Cu 75 °C (30 °C, ≤ 3 CCC): 12 = 25, 10 = 35, 8 = 50, 6 = 65, 4 = 85, 3 = 100, 2 = 115, 1 = 130, 1/0 = 150,
  2/0 = 175, 3/0 = 200, 4/0 = 230, 250 = 255, 350 = 310, 500 = 380 A. Cu 60 °C: 12 = 20, 10 = 30, 8 = 40, 6 = 55, 4 = 70.
  Al 75 °C: 2 = 90, 1/0 = 120, 4/0 = 180, 250 = 205, 500 = 310. Cu caps (240.4(D)): 14 AWG 15 A, 12 20 A, 10 30 A.
- Ambient: k = √((Tc - Ta)/(Tc - 30)) (75 °C at 40 °C 0.88; 90 °C at 40 °C 0.91); rooftop raceway < 7/8 in: +33 °C.
  Grouping (> 3 CCC): 4-6 80 %, 7-9 70 %, 10-20 50 %, 21-30 45 %, 31-40 40 %, > 40 35 %; EGCs never count; neutral
  counts when it carries harmonic/unbalanced current; not for nipples ≤ 24 in.
- Next size up (240.4(B)) only ≤ 800 A; above, ampacity ≥ OCPD. 240.6(A): 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200, 225, 250, 300,
  350, 400, 450, 500, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600, 2000 A. Parallel: ≥ 1/0, identical sets, full-size EGC in each.

## 3. Voltage drop
- 3φ ΔV_LL = √3·I·L·(R cosφ + X sinφ); 1φ ΔV = 2·I·L·(R cosφ + X sinφ); R, X per conductor per length (NEC Ch. 9
  Table 9, by raceway, 75 °C), divided by n parallel sets; % on the same base. Resistive shortcut CM = 2KIL/ΔV (1φ) or
  √3·KIL/ΔV (3φ), K ≈ 12.9 Cu / 21.2 Al Ω·cmil/ft (understates large conductors where X dominates).
- Typical targets (NEC informational notes; binding only if spec/energy code adopts): feeder 2-3 %, branch 3 %, total 5 %;
  IEC 60364-5-52 Annex G: public supply 3 % lighting / 5 % other, private 6 % / 8 %. VD upsizing -> EGC upsized pro rata.

## 4. Short-circuit current and equipment ratings
- Infinite bus: I_sc = I_FL × 100/%Z (1500 kVA, 480 V, 5.75 %: 1804 A -> 31.4 kA). Utility Z_u = V²/S_sc; Z_total =
  Z_u + Z_T + Z_cable. A -7.5 % %Z tolerance raises I_sc ~8 %. Rebase: Z_new = Z_old·(kV_old/kV_new)²·(MVA_new/MVA_old).
  Point-to-point: f = √3·L·I/(C·n·V_LL) (1φ 2·L·I/(C·n·V)), I_end = I_start/(1 + f); C = conductor constant table.
- Motors ≈ 4-6 × FLC for first cycles (4 × in point-to-point); generator ≈ 1/X''d (0.12-0.20 pu). Maximum source is
  conservative for equipment duty, NOT for arc flash or protection sensitivity (run a minimum case too).
- Peak i_p = κ·√2·I_k'', κ = 1.02 + 0.98·e^(-3R/X); ½-cycle asym RMS ≈ I·√(1 + 2e^(-2π/(X/R))). IEC 60909
  I_k'' = c·U_n/(√3·Z_k), c_max 1.05 LV (+6 % tol.) / 1.10 MV and LV +10 %; c_min 0.95 LV, 1.00 MV.
- Test X/R: UL 489 MCCB ≤ 10 kA PF 0.50 (X/R 1.73), 10-20 kA 0.30 (3.18), > 20 kA 0.20 (4.9); LVPCB 0.15 (6.6); MV
  breakers 17; higher system X/R -> derate. Interrupting rating ≥ available fault (110.9); SCCR (110.10, 409.22, 440.4);
  series ratings only as tested/labelled, not with > 1 % motor FLC between devices (240.86); mark available fault and
  date at service (110.24); bus bracing, ATS withstand, busway ratings vs upstream clearing time.

## 5. Protection, selectivity and transformers
- Choose type (fuse J/RK1/L, thermal-magnetic MCCB, electronic LSI/LSIG, LVPCB, relay + breaker), rating, AIC, settings.
  GFPE on solidly grounded wye > 150 V to ground, ≤ 1000 V, disconnect ≥ 1000 A: ≤ 1200 A, ≤ 1 s at 3000 A (230.95).
- Selectivity required: emergency 700.32, legally required standby 701.32, COPS 708.54, elevators 620.62, healthcare
  517. In the instantaneous region prove it with manufacturer selectivity tables (curve non-overlap is not enough);
  fuses typically ≥ 2:1 within one family; breakers via short-time delay without instantaneous, or ZSI.
- Transformer kVA = demand × growth at the cooling class; K-factor for nonlinear loads. Typical %Z: dry 75-500 kVA 3-6 %;
  liquid 750-2500 kVA 5.75 %; X/R ≈ 4-10. Inrush ≈ 8-12 × FLC for 0.1 s; through-fault damage curve IEEE C57.109.
- Taps ±2 × 2.5 % on primary: V_sec = V_pri,actual × V_sec,rated/V_tap; a lower tap voltage RAISES the secondary.
- NEC 450.3(B) (≤ 1000 V): primary only 125 % (< 9 A 167 %, < 2 A 300 %), or primary 250 % + secondary 125 %.
  450.3(A) (> 1000 V, Z ≤ 6 %): primary CB 600 % / fuse 300 %, secondary ≤ 1000 V 125 %; Z 6-10 %: 400 % / 300 %.

## 6. Grounding and bonding (NEC 250)
- EGC Cu by OCPD (250.122): 15 A 14, 20 A 12, 60 A 10, 100 A 8, 200 A 6, 300 A 4, 400 A 3, 500 A 2, 600 A 1, 800 A 1/0,
  1000 A 2/0, 1200 A 3/0, 1600 A 4/0, 2000 A 250, 2500 A 350, 3000 A 400, 4000 A 500 kcmil; full size in each raceway.
- GEC Cu by largest service conductor/equivalent area (250.66): ≤ 2 -> 8; 1-1/0 -> 6; 2/0-3/0 -> 4; to 350 -> 2;
  to 600 -> 1/0; to 1100 -> 2/0; > 1100 -> 3/0; rod-only ≤ 6 AWG, concrete-encased 4 AWG. Bonding jumpers 250.102(C)(1).
- N-G bond only at the service and each separately derived system (250.24, 250.30). Earth is not a fault path; a single
  rod > 25 Ω needs a supplemental electrode ≥ 6 ft away; bond all electrodes present into one system.

## 7. Motor circuits (NEC 430)
- Table FLC (430.247-250), not nameplate, for conductors/OCPD/disconnect; nameplate FLA for overloads. 3φ 460 V: 10 hp
  14, 20 hp 27, 30 hp 40, 50 hp 65, 75 hp 96, 100 hp 124, 150 hp 180, 200 hp 240 A; 230 V ≈ 2 ×; 208 V ≈ 1.1 × 230 V.
- Conductor ≥ 125 % FLC; overload 125 % nameplate (SF ≥ 1.15 or rise ≤ 40 °C) else 115 %. Table 430.52 max % FLC:
  non-time-delay fuse 300, dual-element fuse 175, inverse-time CB 250, instantaneous 800 (1100 Design B energy-
  efficient), next size up allowed. Feeder OCPD ≤ largest branch device + Σ other FLC (430.62). Disconnect ≥ 115 %.
- Starting: DOL 6-8 × FLC (code letter kVA/hp, 430.7(B)); star-delta 1/3 current and torque; autotransformer tap k ->
  k² × DOL; soft starter 2-4 ×; VFD 1-1.5 × (conductors 125 % of drive input rating); torque ∝ V².

## 8. IEC 60364, power factor, checker's list
- I_b ≤ I_n ≤ I_z, I_2 ≤ 1.45·I_z; I_z = I_z0 × C_ambient × C_grouping × C_soil per method (A1-G, Table B.52; ref.
  30 °C air, 20 °C ground, 2.5 K·m/W). Adiabatic S ≥ √(I²t)/k: k = 115 Cu/PVC, 143 Cu/XLPE, 76 Al/PVC, 94 Al/XLPE.
  PE (Table 54.2): S ≤ 16 -> S; 16-35 -> 16; > 35 -> S/2. TN: Z_s ≤ 0.95·U_0/I_a; 230 V final circuits ≤ 32 A 0.4 s,
  distribution 5 s. TT: 0.2 s or R_A·I_Δn ≤ 50 V.
- PF: Q_c = P·(tan φ1 - tan φ2); capacitor conductors ≥ 135 % rated current (460.8); motor-switched ≤ magnetizing kvar.
  Resonance h_r ≈ √(S_sc/Q_c); near 5th/7th with VFDs -> detuned bank (h = 1/√p, 7 % -> 3.78) or filter.
- Common errors: LL vs LN base (208 vs 240); kW vs kVA; 125 % applied twice or never; 90 °C ampacity at 75 °C terminals;
  missing derates; one-way vs round-trip length; nameplate FLA for motor conductors; fault > rating; EGC not full size
  per parallel raceway; downstream N-G bond. State edition, table and every factor used.

---
name: utility-interconnection
description: How utility interconnection, pre-PTO backfeed/energization, witness tests and permission to operate normally work, the reviewer's two-layer check (procedural conditions, then an independent engineering review of the customer's records against the adopted code), walking the operating states, a typical electrical review list, and how a professional determination memo or customer letter is written. Use for any interconnection, energization, PTO, commissioning-approval or utility-reply task.
---

# Utility interconnection, energization and permission to operate (PTO)
Typical lifecycle: application -> screening / studies -> interconnection agreement (ISA) -> construction
(customer facilities under an electrical permit from the authority having jurisdiction, AHJ; utility facilities
under a work order paid by the customer) -> AHJ final inspection and approval -> utility commissioning (metering,
telemetry/RTU end-to-end test, POI protective device acceptance) -> witness test or documented waiver -> written
PTO. Parallel operation before PTO happens only for a witness test under a switching order.
Pre-PTO backfeed / energization for commissioning: utility energizes the customer's transformer and collection
system with the generators disabled and isolated (inverter disconnects open and locked). Normally requires: an
agreement term allowing it, a written request, AHJ final approval of the work being energized, customer
equipment complete and safe to energize (code-compliant wiring, grounding, overcurrent
protection, labels, disconnects), metering set, switching order.
Reviewer's duties:
- Two separate checks: (1) procedural conditions in the agreement, tariff, standards and permit; (2) an
  independent engineering review of the customer's construction records line by line against the code edition
  the permit adopts and the utility standards. Do this even when the AHJ has passed the work; an approval by
  another party is evidence, not proof. A code non-conformance in the record must be corrected and documented
  before energization/PTO.
- Walk the operating states: before PTO (POI device open), during the requested operation, normal parallel
  operation, after a POI trip or utility outage. In each state ask what is energized, what must remain in
  service, and what must be isolated.
- Functions that must keep working (telemetry and RTU, protection relays, communications, remote control, metering):
  trace each one's power supply back to its source (station service, auxiliary transformer, battery/UPS and its
  autonomy) and check it stays energized in every operating state, including while the POI device is open; a
  confirmation obtained in one operating state does not prove another.
- Equipment that will be energized must comply as installed, whatever the generators are doing: generation being
  disabled does not excuse wiring-method, support, labelling, rating or protection defects in the energized part.
- Every finding, adverse or favourable, opens and quotes the clause it relies on and checks its conditions and
  exceptions (a clause that permits the installation removes an apparent violation; a clause not read cannot support
  "compliant").
- Respect the stated scope; where an out-of-scope item depends on something in scope, review the in-scope part.
- Review electrical construction records by NEC article (the edition the permit adopts), plus the utility's
  interconnection standards: 110 (equipment ratings vs available fault current, working space, enclosure ratings,
  markings); 240 (overcurrent protection); 250 (grounding and bonding, equipment grounding and electrode conductors);
  300/310 (wiring methods for the location, support, burial, ampacity with correction factors and terminal ratings);
  312/314 (cabinets, boxes, enclosures); 690 (PV circuits, dc voltage, disconnects, rapid shutdown, labels); 705
  (interconnected sources: point of connection, busbar and conductor rules, disconnects); 706 (energy storage).
Professional reply / memo:
- First sentence answers the question one way or the other (yes / no / not on that date) with the decisive reason.
- For each obstacle: what it is, the exact requirement (document, clause, edition), the evidence in the record,
  what must be done, by whom (name the customer when it is theirs), whether it can be done before the date, and
  what happens if not. Then the path to "yes" (what to resubmit, who re-inspects).
- Items checked and found acceptable: brief list.
- Internal memo vs external letter: an external letter does not cite internal directives or staff deliberations,
  stays short (1-2 pages), and gives one contact. An internal memo can cite internal procedures.
- Do not call a real obstacle a "confirmation", and do not raise an obstacle you have not verified.
- The tracker item (ticket / work package) mirrors the determination: one line per open item with owner and due date.
Before sending: re-check every cited clause and table value against the source; check dates and notice periods
with a script; check that the answer, the open items and the ticket agree; check names and titles against the
contact directory; check that nothing dated after the "as of" date was used.

Hold.**\\n\\n**Basis memo:** `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx` — memorandum to Lena Kovalchuk, SOC Shift Supervisor, from the DER Program Office reviewing engineer (P.E.), dated 07/14/2025.\\n\\n**Decisive item F-1 — AC inverter output conductor ampacity (five circuits AC-C1 to AC-C5).** Canopy Cable Schedule E-201 Rev C (06/24/2025): 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2, 225 A breaker, inverter output 168 A, 40 °C design ambient, 75 °C terminal. NEC 690.8 requires at least 125% × 168 A = 210 A and conductor ampacity at least the 225 A breaker; NEC 110.14(C)/310.15(B)(1) limit the conductor to the 75 °C termination and require the 40 °C correction. On the stricter reading, 230 A × 0.88 = 202.4 A, below 225 A and below 210 A (utilisation 1.112 against the breaker; 1.038 against the 690.8 minimum). The schedule lists 236.6 A in the 90 °C column and 230 A for the 75 °C terminal; on the stricter reading the 75 °C terminal is corrected to 202.4 A. On the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) basis the conductors would be 230 A and would pass, but the record does not state that the AHJ accepted that basis.\\n\\n- **Owner:** Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) through Brantley Electric Company (contractor, permit WEP-25-0317).\\n- **Action:** (a) upsize the five AC inverter output circuits to a conductor whose 75 °C ampacity corrected for 40 °C is at least 225 A (300 kcmil Cu gives 285 × 0.88 = 250.8 A; 250 kcmil gives 255 × 0.88 = 224.4 A and is not enough), with terminations/conduit/voltage drop and the equipment grounding conductor adjusted per NEC 250.122(B), and City of Wrenford re-inspection/final approval; or (b) provide the City of Wrenford's written acceptance of the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) basis (230 A) and update the record. The 225 A breaker cannot be reduced to 200 A because 690.8 requires at least 210 A.\\n- **Verification:** DER Program Office reviewing engineer (P.E.); City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector).\\n- **Due / feasibility:** 08/01/2025 for the corrected record and AHJ acceptance. Not demonstrated on the 07/14/2025 record; the circuits are installed in 2-1/2 in. rigid metal conduit and no conductor replacement or re-inspection is booked.\\n\\n**Decisive item F-2 — SWBD-PV main breaker / T-1 secondary protection.** T-1 is 750 kVA, 13.2 kV to 480Y/277 V, with 480 V secondary full-load current 902 A (Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, 06/24/2025). The SWBD-PV main breaker is 1,200 A, which is 133% of 902 A. NFPA 70-2023 Table 450.3(A) (adopted by City of Wrenford Ordinance 24-118 / permit WEP-25-0317) limits the secondary OCPD to 125% (1,127.6 A) unless the transformer is supervised; a next-higher standard rating may also be available only on a written code basis. The record has no supervised-transformer basis, no written next-higher-standard basis, no T-1 secondary cable-bus rating, and no AHJ finding specifically addressing the 125%/next-higher basis; the 07/02/2025 final approval covers the 1,200 A design.\\n\\n- **Owner:** Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) through Brantley Electric Company (contractor, permit WEP-25-0317).\\n- **Action:** (a) replace the SWBD-PV main with a standard 1,000 A breaker (1,000/902 = 111%); or (b) provide a signed supervised-transformer basis accepted by the City of Wrenford; or (c) provide the written next-higher-standard code basis accepted by the City of Wrenford. Update the equipment schedule and arc-flash label; state the T-1 secondary cable-bus rating; obtain City of Wrenford re-inspection/final approval; deliver the revised record to the DER Program Office.\\n- **Verification:** DER Program Office reviewing engineer (P.E.); City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector); Distribution Protection Engineering to be notified of the corrected customer-side record for information only (POI settings and coordination study remain outside this item).\\n- **Due / feasibility:** 08/01/2025 for the corrected record and AHJ acceptance. Not demonstrated on the 07/14/2025 record (no revised drawing, breaker order/availability, signed basis, cable-bus rating or AHJ re-inspection); hold PTO unless complete by 08/01/2025.\\n\\n**Additional item F-3 — PV labeling.** Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, Labels row records arc-flash labels, source-location plaques, AD-C inverter-disconnect labels, the SWBD-PV main PV-system-disconnect label, and dc power source labels giving only the maximum dc voltage (958.6 V). It does not record the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment required by NEC 690.12(B)(2)(3), or the maximum current/rated output current required on the dc label by NEC 690.53.\\n- **Owner:** Corwyn Realty Partners through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317).\\n- **Action:** install the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment identifying the system and initiator; complete the dc power source labels with the values required by NEC 690.53; provide a photographed as-built label record; City of Wrenford to confirm at re-inspection.\\n- **Due / feasibility:** 08/01/2025. This is a labeling correction; it can be completed and inspected before 08/04/2025.\\n\\n**DER Program Office action:** issue the written notice to Corwyn Realty Partners (attention Nadia Ferreira-Holt) and Brantley Electric Company on 07/15/2025, stating F-1 (AC conductors), F-2 (T-1 secondary main) and F-3 (PV labeling) and the 08/01/2025 deadline.\\n\\n**Pre-PTO confirmation C-1 — CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025.** VX-140C is on CEL-2025-Q2 row 18; CEL-2025-Q3 is planned 07/31/2025. Owner: Evan Solberg, Standards Engineering. Confirm in writing by 08/01/2025 that VX-140C remains listed on the CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025. If delisted, PTO must be held and re-determined.\\n\\n**Pre-PTO confirmation C-2 — live telemetry at the moment of PTO.** TCS-02 §5 requires the SOC Shift Supervisor's confirmation at issuance. Owner: Lena Kovalchuk/SOC. The 07/08/2025 confirmation is evidence only; re-confirm all required points valid at the SCADA operator display on 08/04/2025.\\n\\n**Pre-PTO confirmation C-3 — first parallel operation.** ISA Art. 6.3 / DPS-07 §6.3: SOC to observe and record the first parallel operation with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision after PTO.\\n\\n**Reviewed and acceptable:** ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex executed 09/12/2024 (700 kW ac, feeder ALN-072); witness test WT-0629-01 dated 07/08/2025 all points pass (anti-islanding 0.39–0.46 s vs 2.0 s limit; enter service 301–304 s vs 300 s minimum); CEL-2025-Q2 VX-140C row 18 and certificate VX-CC-25-0522; AHJ final approval WEP-25-0317 dated 07/02/2025; revenue meter RM-0629 set/tested 07/08/2025; DC output and string circuits pass the 40 °C/75 °C check; no Corwyn entry on the 07/14/2025 SOC PTO-Hold Log, hold lists or WO payment ledger.\\n\\n**Out of scope / separate review:** installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser (SCADA/EMS and Distribution Protection Engineering); POI recloser settings and protection coordination study (Distribution Protection Engineering); queue position (Meera Vellanki); system impact study and conditions (Ivo Grantham/DER Planning Group). Nothing else is excluded.\\n\\n**Path to PTO:** Close F-1, F-2 and F-3 and C-1 by 08/01/2025 and confirm C-2 at issuance on 08/04/2025; then PTO may issue on 08/04/2025. If any of F-1, F-2 or F-3 remains open, PTO remains on hold and will be re-determined when the corrected record is complete. INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
Doc no. | RA-2025-07-01
Rev | 1
Date | 07/01/2025
Owner | Regulatory Affairs


TO: DER Program Manager
CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DATE: 07/01/2025
SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking

1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.

/s/
Harriet Ngoyi
Director, Regulatory Affairs
Alleniom Utilities

# Independent review — Corwyn PTO memo and OpenProject work package

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Deliverables reviewed: `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx` (DOCX, 3,889 words, format check passed) and OpenProject work package 47 in project 3 (DER Program Backlog Review). I did not modify either deliverable. Record as-of date 07/14/2025.

The memo's bottom line — **NO, PTO cannot issue on 08/04/2025 on the record as it stands** — is supportable, but not on the basis the memo gives. Two of its three "customer-side items" (F-1 and F-2) are not code violations on the record; they rest on a misreading of NEC 110.14(C) and Table 450.3(A). The memo therefore demands unnecessary conductor and main-breaker replacement and AHJ re-inspection, and its path to "yes" is wrong. The one valid obstacle on the customer's side is F-3 (labeling record), plus the unconfirmed CEL-2025-Q3 listing (C-1) and the unstated T-1 secondary cable-bus rating. Below, most serious first.

---

## 1. BLOCKING — F-2 is not a code violation: the 1,200 A SWBD-PV main is permitted by Table 450.3(A) (next-higher standard rating), and the memo's "125% limit" reads the table incorrectly.

**Requirement.** NFPA 70-2023 Table 450.3(A) (transformer over 1,000 V), as adopted by City of Wrenford Ordinance 24-118 and permit WEP-25-0317; NEC 450.3 notes permitting the next higher standard rating where the calculated value is not a standard rating; NEC 240.6(A) standard ratings.

**What the memo has.** Memo ¶2, ¶15–25 and WP 47: "T-1 750 kVA … 480 V secondary full-load current 902 A (133%); the strict Table 450.3(A) 125% limit is 1,127.6 A, and no supervised or written next-higher-standard basis is on the record." F-2 is called a "hold item, not a documentation comment"; the memo requires Corwyn/Brantley to replace the 1,200 A main with a 1,000 A breaker, or produce a supervised-transformer basis, or produce a written next-higher-standard basis and AHJ acceptance.

**What it should be.** The record values are 750 kVA, 902 A secondary FLA and a 1,200 A main (Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, 06/24/2025, Equipment tab rows T-1 and SWBD-PV). 125% × 902 A = 1,127.6 A is not a standard rating; the next standard rating in NEC 240.6(A) is 1,200 A. Table 450.3(A)'s next-higher-standard note permits the next standard rating; the AHJ's 07/02/2025 final approval is consistent with that. The design is therefore compliant on the 125% reading, and even more clearly compliant if the table's 250% secondary column applies to a non-supervised transformer over 1,000 V (250% × 902 A = 2,255 A). The memo's own working admits "Next standard rating above 1,127.6 A: 1,200 A" (`/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Calculations/Corwyn_Calc.txt`), then treats it as a violation because no "written" basis is on the record. The code note is the basis; the AHJ is not required to issue a written code interpretation.

**Evidence.** E-101 Rev C: T-1 750 kVA, 480 V FLA 902 A; SWBD-PV 1,200 A bus, 1,200 A main; see `/filesystem/Equipment/PXA-2023-0629_Corwyn_Equipment_Schedule.xlsx` (Equipment tab, rows T-1 and SWBD-PV). Computed: 902 × 1.25 = 1,127.5 A; 1,200/902 = 1.330; 1,200 A is the next standard rating. NEC 450.3(A) next-size note; NEC 240.6(A). The memo's own ¶17 says "The calculation is 902 A × 1.25 = 1,127.6 A" and "1,200 A is 133% of 902 A"; its ¶22 option (c) says "1,200 A is the next standard rating above 1,127.6 A." That is the answer to its own objection.

**Consequence.** F-2 must be withdrawn. The demand to replace a compliant 1,200 A main (and to re-inspect and re-approve the switchboard) is unnecessary and could delay PTO beyond 08/04/2025. The only real record gap in this area is that the T-1 secondary cable-bus rating is not stated (see finding 5); that should be a separate, narrow documentation item, not a 125% violation.

---

## 2. BLOCKING — F-1 is not a code violation on the governing 110.14(C)(1)(b)(2) method: 4/0 Cu has 230 A ampacity after the 90 °C correction and the 75 °C cap, above the 225 A breaker and the 210 A 690.8 minimum.

**Requirement.** NFPA 70-2023 110.14(C) (termination temperature limitations; higher-temperature conductors permitted for ampacity adjustment/correction, with ampacity not exceeding the 75 °C ampacity for circuits over 100 A); 310.15(B)(1) (40 °C ambient correction); 690.8(A)(1), (B) (125% of inverter output current; conductor ampacity and OCPD); 240.4.

**What the memo has.** Memo ¶2, ¶8–14 and WP 47: "On the stricter reading of NEC 110.14(C)/310.15(B)(1), the 75 °C terminal ampacity corrected for 40 °C is 230 × 0.88 = 202.4 A, below both the 225 A breaker and the 210 A required by NEC 690.8." The memo calls F-1 "not verified," requires the five AC circuits to be upsized to 300 kcmil Cu (or an AHJ written acceptance of the "alternative" 230 A basis), and says the 225 A breaker cannot be reduced to 200 A.

**What it should be.** The record has 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2, 168 A inverter output, 225 A breaker, 40 °C design ambient; the cable schedule gives 236.6 A in the 90 °C column and 230 A for the 75 °C terminal (E-201 Rev C, Inverter Output Circuits, rows AC-C1 to AC-C5). Under 110.14(C)(1)(b)(2), the 90 °C ampacity is corrected for 40 °C (260 × 0.91 = 236.6 A) and the result is capped at the 75 °C ampacity (230 A): min(236.6, 230) = 230 A. 230 A > 225 A breaker and > 210 A (1.25 × 168 A). The memo's 202.4 A is obtained by applying the 40 °C correction factor 0.88 to the already-75 °C-limited 230 A value — a second, non-code temperature reduction of the terminal cap. The "alternative" the memo says the AHJ must accept is the governing method, not an alternative. The skill guidance (`/tmp/ahpele/skills/electrical-power-design/SKILL.md` §2) states the method: ">100 A -> 75 °C; 90 °C column only as the derating start."

# Independent review — Corwyn PTO memo and OpenProject work package

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Deliverables reviewed: `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx` (DOCX, 3,889 words, format check passed) and OpenProject work package 47 in project 3 (DER Program Backlog Review). I did not modify either deliverable. Record as-of date 07/14/2025.

The memo's bottom line — **NO, PTO cannot issue on 08/04/2025 on the record as it stands** — is supportable, but not on the basis the memo gives. Two of its three "customer-side items" (F-1 and F-2) are not code violations on the record; they rest on a misreading of NEC 110.14(C) and Table 450.3(A). The memo therefore demands unnecessary conductor and main-breaker replacement and AHJ re-inspection, and its path to "yes" is wrong. The one valid obstacle on the customer's side is F-3 (labeling record), plus the unconfirmed CEL-2025-Q3 listing (C-1) and the unstated T-1 secondary cable-bus rating. Below, most serious first.

---

## 1. BLOCKING — F-2 is not a code violation: the 1,200 A SWBD-PV main is permitted by Table 450.3(A) (next-higher standard rating), and the memo's "125% limit" reads the table incorrectly.

**Requirement.** NFPA 70-2023 Table 450.3(A) (transformer over 1,000 V), as adopted by City of Wrenford Ordinance 24-118 and permit WEP-25-0317; NEC 450.3 notes permitting the next higher standard rating where the calculated value is not a standard rating; NEC 240.6(A) standard ratings.

**What the memo has.** Memo ¶2, ¶15–25 and WP 47: "T-1 750 kVA … 480 V secondary full-load current 902 A (133%); the strict Table 450.3(A) 125% limit is 1,127.6 A, and no supervised or written next-higher-standard basis is on the record." F-2 is called a "hold item, not a documentation comment"; the memo requires Corwyn/Brantley to replace the 1,200 A main with a 1,000 A breaker, or produce a supervised-transformer basis, or produce a written next-higher-standard basis and AHJ acceptance.

**What it should be.** The record values are 750 kVA, 902 A secondary FLA and a 1,200 A main (Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, 06/24/2025, Equipment tab rows T-1 and SWBD-PV). The memo's 125% figure is the correct 2020/2023 Table 450.3(A) secondary limit for a transformer over 1,000 V with a secondary of 1,000 V or less (125% any location; 250% supervised location). But 125% × 902 A = 1,127.6 A is not a standard rating; the next standard rating in NEC 240.6(A) is 1,200 A. Table 450.3(A)'s next-higher-standard-rating note — "Where the calculated value does not correspond to a standard rating of a fuse or nonadjustable circuit breaker, the next higher standard rating shall be permitted" — permits the 1,200 A main. The AHJ's 07/02/2025 final approval is consistent with that. The memo's own working admits "Next standard rating above 1,127.6 A: 1,200 A" (`/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Calculations/Corwyn_Calc.txt`), then treats it as a violation because no "written" basis is on the record. The code note is the basis; the AHJ is not required to issue a written code interpretation. If the table's 250% supervised-location value were applied, the 1,200 A main would be even further inside the limit (250% × 902 A = 2,255 A). Either way, F-2 is not a violation.

**Evidence.** E-101 Rev C: T-1 750 kVA, 480 V FLA 902 A; SWBD-PV 1,200 A bus, 1,200 A main; see `/filesystem/Equipment/PXA-2023-0629_Corwyn_Equipment_Schedule.xlsx` (Equipment tab, rows T-1 and SWBD-PV). Computed: 902 × 1.25 = 1,127.5 A; 1,200/902 = 1.330; 1,200 A is the next standard rating. NEC 450.3(A) next-size note; NEC 240.6(A). The memo's own ¶17 says "The calculation is 902 A × 1.25 = 1,127.6 A" and "1,200 A is 133% of 902 A"; its ¶22 option (c) says "1,200 A is the next standard rating above 1,127.6 A." That is the answer to its own objection.

**Consequence.** F-2 must be withdrawn. The demand to replace a compliant 1,200 A main (and to re-inspect and re-approve the switchboard) is unnecessary and could delay PTO beyond 08/04/2025. The only real record gap in this area is that the T-1 secondary cable-bus rating is not stated (see finding 5); that should be a separate, narrow documentation item, not a 125% violation. A change of the customer's main breaker would also change the fault/coordination basis that Distribution Protection Engineering used for the POI recloser; the memo treats DPE as "information only" (¶24), which understates that interface. Since F-2 is not a violation, the correct action is to leave the 1,200 A main alone and notify DPE of nothing.

## 2. BLOCKING — F-1 is not a code violation on the governing 110.14(C)(1)(b)(2) method: 4/0 Cu has 230 A ampacity after the 90 °C correction and the 75 °C cap, above the 225 A breaker and the 210 A 690.8 minimum.

**Requirement.** NFPA 70-2023 110.14(C) (termination temperature limitations; higher-temperature conductors permitted for ampacity adjustment/correction, with ampacity not exceeding the 75 °C ampacity for circuits over 100 A); 310.15(B)(1) (40 °C ambient correction); 690.8(A)(1), (B) (125% of inverter output current; conductor ampacity and OCPD); 240.4.

**What the memo has.** Memo ¶2, ¶8–14 and WP 47: "On the stricter reading of NEC 110.14(C)/310.15(B)(1), the 75 °C terminal ampacity corrected for 40 °C is 230 × 0.88 = 202.4 A, below both the 225 A breaker and the 210 A required by NEC 690.8." The memo calls F-1 "not verified," requires the five AC circuits to be upsized to 300 kcmil Cu (or an AHJ written acceptance of the "alternative" 230 A basis), and says the 225 A breaker cannot be reduced to 200 A.

**What it should be.** The record has 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2, 168 A inverter output, 225 A breaker, 40 °C design ambient; the cable schedule gives 236.6 A in the 90 °C column and 230 A for the 75 °C terminal (E-201 Rev C, Inverter Output Circuits, rows AC-C1 to AC-C5). Under 110.14(C)(1)(b)(2), the 90 °C ampacity is corrected for 40 °C (260 × 0.91 = 236.6 A) and the result is capped at the 75 °C ampacity (230 A): min(236.6, 230) = 230 A. 230 A > 225 A breaker and > 210 A (1.25 × 168 A). The memo's 202.4 A is obtained by applying the 40 °C correction factor 0.88 to the already-75 °C-limited 230 A value — a second, non-code temperature reduction of the terminal cap. The "alternative" the memo says the AHJ must accept is the governing method, not an alternative. The skill guidance (`/tmp/ahpele/skills/electrical-power-design/SKILL.md` §2) states the method: ">100 A -> 75 °C; 90 °C column only as the derating start."

**Evidence.** E-201 Rev C: 3 × 1/C 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2, 225 A breaker, 168 A, "Ampacity at 40 °C, 90 °C column 236.6 A", "Terminal rating 75 °C 230 A", lengths 96–160 m, voltage drop 1.16–1.93%. Computed: 260 × 0.91 = 236.6 A; min(236.6, 230) = 230 A; 230/225 = 1.022; 230/210 = 1.095. The memo's own ¶11 concedes: "On the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) reading, the ampacity is 230 A and the conductors would pass." That is the code reading. The AHJ's 07/02/2025 final approval is evidence that the installed 4/0 design was accepted; the memo dismisses it without identifying a code clause that requires the AHJ to state a basis.

**Consequence.** F-1 must be withdrawn. The five 4/0 circuits do not need to be replaced with 300 kcmil; the 225 A breaker is not undersized; no AHJ re-inspection is required for this item. The memo's "worst-case utilisation 1.112" is an artefact of the double correction. The record does not need a written AHJ acceptance of the 230 A basis.

## 3. MAJOR — Because F-1 and F-2 are wrong, the memo's "three customer-side items" and its path to "yes" are wrong; the only valid customer-side hold is F-3, with C-1 and the cable-bus rating.

**Requirement.** Instruction: tell Lena whether PTO can issue on 08/04/2025 "one way or the other, and give the basis"; for anything that stands in the way, say what it is, what it rests on, what has to be done and by whom, and whether it can be done before that date. Backlog Review Directive DIR-2025-0627: "Every disposition must be tariff-defensible. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, or operating guideline that supports the action. If the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready."

**What the memo has.** A "No" determination based on three items (F-1, F-2, F-3), with F-1 and F-2 carrying the bulk of the analysis and the 08/01/2025 action list. The memo says "Three customer-side items are not verified" and "F-1, F-2 and F-3 must be closed."

**What it should be.** A "No" determination can still be correct, but the basis must be the actual record gaps: (i) F-3 — the E-101 Labels row does not show the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment or the full 690.53 dc label content; (ii) C-1 — CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025, before the requested PTO date, so the VX-140C listing on the edition in force on 08/04/2025 must be confirmed; and (iii) the T-1 secondary cable-bus rating is not stated in E-101, so the 1,200 A main's protection of the secondary cable bus is not verified. F-1 and F-2 should be removed, not merely softened. The memo's recommendation to issue a notice citing F-1/F-2 and to require conductor/breaker replacement should be reissued with the correct items.

**Evidence.** Memo ¶2 (first sentence), ¶3 ("F-1, F-2 and F-3 must be closed"), ¶47 (notice stating F-1, F-2, F-3), WP 47 description (same). The false F-1/F-2 analysis is findings 1–2 above. The valid F-3 record gap is finding 4. The cable-bus gap is finding 5. DIR-2025-0627 ground rules (06/27/2025).

**Consequence.** The final answer "No" is not wrong on the record, but it is over-determined for the wrong reasons; the action list is not tariff-defensible as written and imposes unnecessary work on Corwyn. A senior reviewer should not let the memo go out with F-1/F-2 as stated.

## 4. MAJOR — F-3 is a valid record gap, but the memo overstates it as a proven "labeling non-conformance" and cites the rapid-shutdown plaque clause imprecisely.

**Requirement.** NFPA 70-2023 690.12 (rapid shutdown; plaque at the service equipment identifying the rapid shutdown system and its initiator); 690.53 (dc power source label with maximum voltage, maximum current, maximum rated output current and maximum rated output power). The permit adopts NFPA 70-2023 (WEP-25-0317).

**What the memo has.** Memo ¶26–32: "The PV labeling record does not show the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment or the full dc power source label content required by NEC 690.12 and 690.53." "This is a labeling non-conformance; it can be corrected without changing the electrical design." The memo cites "Section 690.12(B)(2)(3)." It requires the plaque, the full dc label values, a photographed as-built label record, and City of Wrenford confirmation at re-inspection.

**What it should be.** The record supports a "not verified" finding, not a proven field non-conformance. E-101 Rev C, Labels row (row 12) records: arc-flash labels; a SWBD-PV label with nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date; the multiple-source marking; "a plaque at SWBD-PV and at PSW-1 showing the location of each power source and its disconnect"; AD-C labels; the SWBD-PV main marked as the PV system disconnect; and "a dc power source label at each inverter dc input and each combiner giving the maximum dc voltage, 958.6 V." It does not record a rapid-shutdown plaque identifying the rapid shutdown system and its initiator at the service equipment, and the dc labels are recorded as giving only the maximum voltage. The String Schedule E-301 records module-level rapid shutdown devices, the transmitter at SWBD-PV and the initiator at the SWBD-PV main, but not a service-equipment plaque. That is a record gap. The memo should say "the record does not demonstrate" (which it does in ¶29), not "the record does not show" plus "This is a labeling non-conformance" — the latter asserts a field defect that has not been inspected. The action (install/complete labels, photograph, AHJ confirm) is appropriate, and it is the one customer-side item that is genuinely capable of being closed before 08/04/2025. The clause citation should be checked against the adopted 2023 edition; 690.12(B)(2)(3) is not the usual citation for the service-equipment plaque (the plaque/marking requirement is 690.12(B)(2) or 690.12(D), depending on edition), and a wrong subsection is a citation error in a memo that otherwise insists on exact clauses.

**Evidence.** E-101 Rev C Labels row; E-301 Rev C "Rapid shutdown" row; Wintbrook one-line diagram label row (a comparable complete label record: "Rapid shutdown sign at the service identifying the rapid shutdown system and its initiator; a dc power source label at each dc disconnect giving the maximum dc voltage, 956 V") — the Corwyn E-101 record lacks the equivalent rapid-shutdown sign. Memo ¶26–32.

**Consequence.** F-3 remains a valid reason to hold; the memo's conclusion is right, but its characterization is stronger than the record. The memo should distinguish "record not verified" from "installed label missing," and should cite the exact 2023 clause.

---

## 5. MAJOR — The T-1 secondary cable-bus rating is not stated in the record, and the memo bundles this real gap into the false F-2 instead of treating it as a standalone pre-PTO item.

**Requirement.** NEC 240.4 / 450.3 (secondary conductors and cable bus protected by the secondary OCPD); NEC 705.12 (interconnected source busbar and conductor rules); ISA Article 4.1 (conformity with the code and Company standards). The permit adopts NEC 2023.

**What the memo has.** Memo ¶17: "The T-1 secondary cable bus rating is also not stated in the record." F-2's action says "The revised equipment schedule must also state the T-1 secondary cable bus rating and show that the 1,000 A (or documented 1,200 A) main protects it." But F-2's headline is the 125% violation; if F-2 is withdrawn, the cable-bus gap disappears from the action list. The memo's "Items reviewed and found acceptable" does not list the cable bus as a separate open item.

**What it should be.** E-101 Rev C, Equipment tab, row T-1: "Pad-mounted, liquid-filled; impedance 5.75 %; secondary cable bus to SWBD-PV" — no rating, no conductor size, no ampacity. The SWBD-PV main is 1,200 A. The record therefore does not show that the secondary cable bus is rated at least 1,200 A (or that it is otherwise protected). This is a real "not verified" item independent of the 125% question. The memo should list it as a standalone pre-PTO record item: Corwyn/Brantley to provide the cable-bus rating and the protection basis; the DER Program Office to verify. It should not be used to support a 125% violation.

**Evidence.** E-101 Rev C row T-1; row SWBD-PV (1,200 A main); memo ¶17 and ¶23. The record has no cable-bus rating in any Corwyn schedule.

**Consequence.** Even after F-1/F-2 are withdrawn, the memo cannot say the customer's 480 V interconnection is fully verified until the cable-bus rating is on file. This is a genuine, narrow hold item. It can likely be closed by a revised E-101 or a cable-bus datasheet before 08/04/2025.

---

## 6. MAJOR — The memo reviews the RTU station-service/UPS ride-through, which is part of the RTU installation and configuration under separate review, and reaches an unverified conclusion on an assumed load.

**Requirement.** Instruction: "Four matters are under separate review and are not for this memo: the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser at the site (SCADA/EMS Engineering and Distribution Protection Engineering)… Nothing else is under separate review." TCS-02 §3.4 (4-hour UPS ride-through).

**What the memo has.** Memo ¶41 (table 4, "RTU station service"): "PP-1 circuit 1 feeds the utility RTU enclosure through a 1.5 kVA Corvane OL-1500R UPS; Equipment Schedule E-101 states 5.5 h at the RTU load. TCS-02 §3.4 requires a minimum 4 h outage ride-through. The Corvane datasheet gives 4.4 h at 40 W and 3.88 h at 50 W on a new battery; with the datasheet 20% end-of-battery-life derating, 4 h is met at about 31 W or less. The actual RTU load is not stated; this is part of the RTU interface under separate review and is not a separate condition of this memo."

**What it should be.** The memo should not analyze or conclude on the RTU UPS at all; that is the RTU installation/configuration under separate review. If it mentions the UPS for context, it must not state a ride-through conclusion ("4 h is met at about 31 W or less") based on an assumed load that the record does not state. The record's E-101 says "5.5 h at the RTU load" but does not state the load; the Corvane datasheet's 20% derating gives 4.40 × 0.8 = 3.52 h at 40 W and 3.88 × 0.8 = 3.10 h at 50 W, so 4 h is not met at 40 W after derating. The memo's "about 31 W or less" is an interpolation, not a record value. This is an out-of-scope conclusion that could be wrong and is not needed for the PTO determination.

**Evidence.** Memo ¶41; TCS-02 §3.4; Corvane OL-1500R datasheet (`/filesystem/Equipment/Corvane_OL-1500R_UPS_Data_Sheet.pdf`): usable 376 Wh, 40 W standing loss, 4.40 h at 40 W, 3.88 h at 50 W, "Derate 20 percent at end of battery life"; E-101 PP-1 row: "5.5 h at the RTU load" with no load value. The instruction's separate-review list includes the RTU installation and configuration.

**Consequence.** Remove the RTU UPS analysis from the memo (or reduce it to a one-line "under separate review, not decided here"). If the RTU UPS is inadequate, that is a SCADA/EMS finding, not this memo's; if it is adequate, the memo's assumed 31 W is not evidence. The scope exclusion must be respected both ways.

---

## 7. MAJOR — The memo does not line-review the customer's installation against the NEC articles the permit adopts (110, 240, 250, 300/310, 312/314, 690, 705); several required record items are absent or unverified.

**Requirement.** Instruction: review the record line by line, "materials, methods, labels, conditions, not only the calculations"; the utility-interconnection skill's review list: 110 (equipment ratings, working space, enclosure ratings, markings), 240 (overcurrent protection), 250 (grounding/bonding), 300/310 (wiring methods, ampacity), 312/314 (cabinets/enclosures), 690 (PV circuits, dc voltage, disconnects, rapid shutdown, labels), 705 (interconnected sources, busbar/conductor rules, disconnects). ISA Article 4.1 requires conformity with the code in effect.

**What the memo has.** Memo ¶41 table 4 is a short "Items reviewed and found acceptable" list: ISA/project identity; witness test; inverter certification; AC/DC circuits; AHJ approval; RTU station service; metering; payment/holds. It does not contain a line-review table of E-101/E-201/E-301/E-401 against the NEC articles, and it does not identify the following record gaps (separate from F-1/F-2/F-3):
- E-101 T-1 secondary cable-bus rating (finding 5);
- inverter working space: E-101 row INV-C1 to INV-C5 says "working space faces the island walkway" but gives no depth/width/height; NEC 110.26 requires 1 m depth, 750 mm width and 2 m height for 480 V equipment. The record does not demonstrate it; the AHJ final approval is evidence, not proof.
- the SWBD-PV main breaker's lockable-open/visible-break provision: E-101 says "the SWBD-PV main marked as the PV system disconnect" but not that it is lockable; NEC 690.13(A) requires the PV system disconnecting means to be lockable open. The AD-C disconnects are recorded as lockable visible-break; the main is not.
- the 13.2 kV primary conductors from PSW-1 to the POI: E-101 gives PSW-1 (15 kV, 200 A, 65E fuses) and T-1 primary FLA 32.8 A, but no primary conductor size/ampacity; the ISA Exhibit A says the customer's 13.2 kV primary conductors run from the POI to PSW-1. DPE's DER-side protection review may cover this (separate review), but the memo does not say so.
- arc-flash label content: E-101 says the SWBD-PV label gives nominal voltage, available

The valid F-3 record gap is finding 4. The cable-bus gap is finding 5. DIR-2025-0627 ground rules (06/27/2025).

## 4. MAJOR — F-3 is a valid record gap, but the memo overstates it as a proven "labeling non-conformance" and cites the rapid-shutdown plaque clause imprecisely.

**Requirement.** NFPA 70-2023 690.12 (rapid shutdown; plaque at the service equipment identifying the rapid shutdown system and its initiator); 690.53 (dc power source label with maximum voltage, maximum current, maximum rated output current and maximum rated output power). The permit adopts NFPA 70-2023 (WEP-25-0317).

**What the memo has.** Memo ¶26–32: "The PV labeling record does not show the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment or the full dc power source label content required by NEC 690.12 and 690.53." "This is a labeling non-conformance; it can be corrected without changing the electrical design." The memo cites "Section 690.12(B)(2)(3)." It requires the plaque, the full dc label values, a photographed as-built label record, and City of Wrenford confirmation at re-inspection.

**What it should be.** The record supports a "not verified" finding, not a proven field non-conformance. E-101 Rev C, Labels row (row 12) records: arc-flash labels; a SWBD-PV label with nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date; the multiple-source marking; "a plaque at SWBD-PV and at PSW-1 showing the location of each power source and its disconnect"; AD-C labels; the SWBD-PV main marked as the PV system disconnect; and "a dc power source label at each inverter dc input and each combiner giving the maximum dc voltage, 958.6 V." It does not record a rapid-shutdown plaque identifying the rapid shutdown system and its initiator at the service equipment, and the dc labels are recorded as giving only the maximum voltage. The String Schedule E-301 records module-level rapid shutdown devices, the transmitter at SWBD-PV and the initiator at the SWBD-PV main, but not a service-equipment plaque. That is a record gap. The memo should say "the record does not demonstrate" (which it does in ¶29), not "the record does not show" plus "This is a labeling non-conformance" — the latter asserts a field defect that has not been inspected. The action (install/complete labels, photograph, AHJ confirm) is appropriate, and it is the one customer-side item that is genuinely capable of being closed before 08/04/2025. This is a real "not verified" item independent of the 125% question. The memo should list it as a standalone pre-PTO record item: Corwyn/Brantley to provide the cable-bus rating and the protection basis; the DER Program Office to verify. It should not be used to support a 125% violation.

**Evidence.** E-101 Rev C row T-1; row SWBD-PV (1,200 A main); memo ¶17 and ¶23. The record has no cable-bus rating in any Corwyn schedule.

## 6. MAJOR — The memo reviews the RTU station-service/UPS ride-through, which is part of the RTU installation and configuration under separate review, and reaches an unverified conclusion on an assumed load.

**Requirement.** Instruction: "Four matters are under separate review and are not for this memo: the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser at the site (SCADA/EMS Engineering and Distribution Protection Engineering)… Nothing else is under separate review." TCS-02 §3.4 (4-hour UPS ride-through).

**What the memo has.** Memo ¶41 (table 4, "RTU station service"): "PP-1 circuit 1 feeds the utility RTU enclosure through a 1.5 kVA Corvane OL-1500R UPS; Equipment Schedule E-101 states 5.5 h at the RTU load. TCS-02 §3.4 requires a minimum 4 h outage ride-through. The Corvane datasheet gives 4.4 h at 40 W and 3.88 h at 50 W on a new battery; with the datasheet 20% end-of-battery-life derating, 4 h is met at about 31 W or less. The actual RTU load is not stated; this is part of the RTU interface under separate review and is not a separate condition of this memo."

**What it should be.** The memo should not analyze or conclude on the RTU UPS at all; that is the RTU installation/configuration under separate review. If it mentions the UPS for context, it must not state a ride-through conclusion ("4 h is met at about 31 W or less") based on an assumed load that the record does not state. The record's E-101 says "5.5 h at the RTU load" but does not state the load; the Corvane datasheet's 20% derating gives 4.40 × 0.8 = 3.52 h at 40 W and 3.88 × 0.8 = 3.10 h at 50 W, so 4 h is not met at 40 W after derating. The instruction's separate-review list includes the RTU installation and configuration.

**Consequence.** Remove the RTU UPS analysis from the memo (or reduce it to a one-line "under separate review, not decided here"). If the RTU UPS is inadequate, that is a SCADA/EMS finding, not this memo's; if it is adequate, the memo's assumed 31 W is not evidence. The scope exclusion must be respected both ways.

---

F-2 is called a "hold item, not a documentation comment"; the memo requires Corwyn/Brantley to replace the 1,200 A main with a 1,000 A breaker, or produce a supervised-transformer basis, or produce a written next-higher-standard basis and AHJ acceptance.

**What it should be.** The record values are 750 kVA, 902 A secondary FLA and a 1,200 A main (Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, 06/24/2025, Equipment tab rows T-1 and SWBD-PV). The memo's 125% figure is the correct 2020/2023 Table 450.3(A) secondary limit for a transformer over 1,000 V with a secondary of 1,000 V or less (125% any location; 250% supervised location). But 125% × 902 A = 1,127.6 A is not a standard rating; the next standard rating in NEC 240.6(A) is 1,200 A. Table 450.3(A)'s next-higher-standard-rating note — "Where the calculated value does not correspond to a standard rating of a fuse or nonadjustable circuit breaker, the next higher standard rating shall be permitted" — permits the 1,200 A main. The AHJ's 07/02/2025 final approval is consistent with that. The memo's own working admits "Next standard rating above 1,127.6 A: 1,200 A" (`/tmp/ahpele/corpus/Calculations/Corwyn_Calc.txt`), then treats it as a violation because no "written" basis is on the record. The code note is the basis; the AHJ is not required to issue a written code interpretation. The note is written for a fuse or nonadjustable circuit breaker; if the SWBD-PV main is an adjustable electronic breaker, the trip setting can be set at 1,127.6 A or less, and the 1,200 A frame rating is not the operative limit. The record does not state the trip setting; that is a separate record gap, not a 133% violation. If the table's 250% supervised-location value were applied, the 1,200 A main would be even further inside the limit (250% × 902 A = 2,255 A). Either way, F-2 is not a violation.

**Evidence.** E-101 Rev C: T-1 750 kVA, 480 V FLA 902 A; SWBD-PV 1,200 A bus, 1,200 A main; see `/filesystem/Equipment/PXA-2023-0629_Corwyn_Equipment_Schedule.xlsx` (Equipment tab, rows T-1 and SWBD-PV). Computed: 902 × 1.25 = 1,127.5 A; 1,200/902 = 1.330; 1,200 A is the next standard rating. NEC 450.3(A) next-size note; NEC 240.6(A). The memo's F-2 working says "The calculation is 902 A × 1.25 = 1,127.6 A" and "1,200 A is 133% of 902 A"; its F-2 option (c) says "1,200 A is the next standard rating above 1,127.6 A." That is the answer to its own objection.

**Consequence.** F-2 must be withdrawn. The demand to replace a compliant 1,200 A main (and to re-inspect and re-approve the switchboard) is unnecessary and could delay PTO beyond 08/04/2025. The only real record gap in this area is that the T-1 secondary cable-bus rating is not stated (see finding 5); that should be a separate, narrow documentation item, not a 125% violation. A change of the customer's main breaker would also change the fault/coordination basis that Distribution Protection Engineering used for the POI recloser; the memo treats DPE as "information only" (¶24), which understates that interface. Since F-2 is not a violation, the correct action is to leave the 1,200 A main alone and notify DPE of nothing.
