1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
•
IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
•
IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
•
IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
•
ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.


--- page 2 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 2
•
Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
•
Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
communications shall not defeat local protection.
Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.


--- page 3 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 3
5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
clearance holds.
6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
premises.
4.3 DER-Side Protection
DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.
4.4 Grounding
The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.
4.5 Anti-Islanding
The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.
5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
(a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
recloser.
(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
site's operating procedure.
(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
prior to energization.
5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.
5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.
5.4 Reclosing Blocking
Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the

affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
5.5 Settings Governance
All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
the field without a written revision order.
6. TESTING
6.1 Factory Acceptance
The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
shipment.
6.2 Site Acceptance
Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
by Alleniom Utilities:
1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
and reset.
4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.
6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.
6.4 Periodic Testing
The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.
6.5 Post-Event Testing
Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.
End of DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard. Distribution: Alleniom Standards Engineering master file;
Distribution Protection Engineering; Distribution Operations; DER Program Office; APUC filing (informational).
Engineering and recorded in the site's interconnection file.

Facilities at or above the TCS-02 program threshold shall provide real-time monitoring and control integration through
a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system
operations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5
for the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.

relay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the
control-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.
§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
permitted for capacity or POI changes.
Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
invoking this section.
Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
executed.
Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
interconnection after ISA execution shall:
1.  Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
2.  File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
3.  Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
applicant as involving new or existing equipment.
Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.
Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.
§8 Records and Compliance
Interconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the
retention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this
standard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral
Procedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.

standard and another Alleniom operating standard encountered in screening or study is referred to per-site
engineering determination under ERP-9 §3.

Approving authority: Manager, Standards Engineering
§1   PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.
§2   SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
•
a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
•
b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
•
c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
•
d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com

TCS-02
Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common
coupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the
aggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.
§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1   Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.3   Functional requirements
Each RTU shall, at minimum:
•
a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
•
b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
processors over an approved communications path (§4).
•
c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
restoration.
•
d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.
•
e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.
§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5   Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.
§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification
§3.2   Approved models
The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).


--- page 3 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021
Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 3
Telemetry & Communications Standard
TCS-02
Prior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end
point-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,
exercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.
Commissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.
§4   COMMUNICATIONS
§4.1   Communications transport
The RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by
SCADA/EMS Engineering:
•
a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or
•
b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or
•
c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held
by Alleniom.
Customer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.
Where site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for
interconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.
§4.2   SCADA protocol
The RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure
Authentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration
parameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —
shall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§4.3   Availability
The end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a
monthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent
loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be
corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
equipment.
§4.4   Address and IP management
All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate
connections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration
record.
§5   TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE
§5.   ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.
This requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under
DIS-01 §3.4.
Live telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:
•
a.   Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;

b.   Communicating with Alleniom SCADA over an approved transport (§4) at the refresh
cadence required by §6; and
•
c.   Presenting all required data points (§6) as valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged
bad-quality) at the SCADA operator display at the moment Permission to Operate (PTO) is
issued.
Compliance with §5 is confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift at the time PTO is
requested. The SOC's confirmation is recorded against the interconnection file. PTO shall not be

§6   DATA POINTS AND REFRESH RATES
§6.1   Required data points
Each in-scope DER site shall present, at minimum, the following analog and status points to

§6.2   Refresh rates


--- page 5 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021
Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 5
Telemetry & Communications Standard
TCS-02
Analog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3
Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than
every sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an
integrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be
reported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.
§6.3   Data quality
Every value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,
restart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the
RTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be
reported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.
§6.4   Retention
Alleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six
(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,
engineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.
§7   CYBERSECURITY
§7.1   Applicability
The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.
§7.2   Access control
Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.
§7.3   Communications security
DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.
§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management
RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following
the Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a
cryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or
reconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.
§7.5   Logging and monitoring
The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
procedure.


--- page 6 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021
Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 6
Telemetry & Communications Standard
TCS-02
§7.6   Physical security
The RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any
physical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a
status point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.
§7.7   Incident response
The customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its
enclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and
utility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to
SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§7.8   Decommissioning
At end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.
Customer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided
credentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.
End of TCS-02.

ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1.
The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2.
Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3.
Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4.
Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.
Alleniom Utilities · DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com


--- page 2 ---
ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office
Page 2
5.
The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:
•
the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;
•
for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;


--- page 3 ---
ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office
Page 3
•
for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
date;
•
the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
the CEL listing relied upon;
•
correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
test-plan negotiation.
The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
against the current CEL edition.
End of procedure. See DIS-01 Rev 4 for interconnection standards, TCS-02 for telemetry requirements, and the
current CEL edition for the list of qualifying equipment. Revisions to this procedure are issued by Standards
Engineering and take effect on the date shown in the document-control block above.

exit_code=0
p='/tmp/ahpele/make_memo.py'
s=open(p).read()

# Replace first two paragraphs
start=s.index('p("Permission to Operate cannot issue for Corwyn Office Complex PV on 08/04/2025 on the record before me.')
end=s.index('# --- 2. Basis ---', start)
new_first='''p("Permission to Operate cannot issue for Corwyn Office Complex PV on 08/04/2025 on the record before me. Two customer-side design items are not verified. First, the five AC inverter output circuits use 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2 conductors on 225 A breakers; at the 40 °C design ambient the schedule gives 236.6 A in the 90 °C column and a 75 °C terminal rating of 230 A. On the stricter reading of NEC 110.14(C)/310.15(B)(1), the 75 °C terminal ampacity corrected for 40 °C is 230 × 0.88 = 202.4 A, below both the 225 A breaker and the 210 A required by NEC 690.8 (125% × 168 A). The record does not state that the AHJ accepted the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) basis of 230 A; on that alternative the conductors would pass. Second, the SWBD-PV main breaker is 1,200 A on a 750 kVA transformer whose 480 V secondary full-load current is 902 A (133%); the strict Table 450.3(A) 125% limit is 1,127.6 A, and no supervised or written next-higher-standard basis is on the record. The City of Wrenford's final approval of 07/02/2025 and the completed witness test do not cure either item.", bold=False)
p("The witness test, inverter certification and telemetry record are otherwise in order for the inverter protective functions. Both F-1 and F-2 must be closed, or their AHJ basis documented, before the facility is energized. A separate pre-issuance check of the Certified Equipment List edition in force on 08/04/2025 (CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025) is also required; it is not a present non-conformance but it must be closed before issuance.", italic=False)

'''
s=s[:start]+new_first+s[end:]

# Replace Section 3 block
start=s.index('doc.add_heading("3. What stands in the way:')
end=s.index('# --- 4. Pre-issuance confirmations ---', start)
new_sec='''doc.add_heading("3. What stands in the way: F-1 — AC inverter output conductor ampacity; F-2 — SWBD-PV main breaker", level=1)
p("F-1. The AC inverter output conductors are not verified at the 40 °C design ambient.", bold=True)
p("Requirement. NEC 690.8(A)(1) and (B) require the inverter output conductors to carry 125% of the inverter continuous output current (1.25 × 168 A = 210 A) and to be protected by the 225 A breaker. NEC 110.14(C) limits the conductor to the lowest connected termination temperature (75 °C), and NEC 310.15(B)(1) requires the 40 °C ambient correction. The stricter reading applied here corrects the 75 °C terminal ampacity: 230 A × 0.88 = 202.4 A.")
p("What it rests on. Canopy Cable Schedule E-201 Rev C (06/24/2025), rows AC-C1 to AC-C5: 3 × 1/C 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2 plus 1/C 4 AWG Cu ground, 225 A breaker at SWBD-PV, inverter output 168 A; the schedule columns are \\"Ampacity at 40 °C, 90 °C column 236.6 A\\" and \\"Terminal rating 75 °C 230 A\\"; lengths are 96 to 160 m and voltage drop 1.16% to 1.93%.")
p("Calculation. 4/0 Cu 75 °C ampacity is 230 A; the 40 °C correction is 0.88, giving 202.4 A. That is below the 225 A breaker and below the 210 A required by 690.8. Utilisation is 225/202.4 = 1.112 against the breaker and 210/202.4 = 1.038 against the 690.8 minimum. On the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) reading, the ampacity is 230 A and the conductors would pass; the record does not state which basis the AHJ accepted.")
p("What to do. Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must either (a) upsize the five AC inverter output circuits to a conductor whose 75 °C ampacity corrected for 40 °C is at least 225 A (300 kcmil Cu gives 285 × 0.88 = 250.8 A; 250 kcmil gives 255 × 0.88 = 224.4 A and is not enough), with terminations, conduit and voltage drop updated, and obtain AHJ re-inspection and final approval; or (b) provide the City of Wrenford's written acceptance of the alternative min(90 °C corrected, 75 °C table) basis (230 A) and update the record. The 225 A breaker cannot be reduced to 200 A because 690.8 requires at least 210 A.")
p("Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor) for the design, conductors, terminations and AHJ submission; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for re-inspection and final approval; the DER Program Office for verification.")
p("Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Not on the record. The five circuits are installed in 2-1/2 in. rigid metal conduit; conductor replacement, termination changes and AHJ re-inspection are not on the record or booked. A written AHJ acceptance of the alternative basis may be achievable, but the record does not contain it. To keep 08/04/2025, Corwyn must complete (a) or (b) and deliver the AHJ acceptance to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025. Otherwise PTO should be held and re-determined when the corrected record is complete.")
p("F-2. The SWBD-PV main breaker is not verified against the T-1 secondary overcurrent-protection limit.", bold=True)
p("Requirement. NFPA 70-2023, Table 450.3(A) (adopted by the City of Wrenford by Ordinance 24-118 and made part of permit WEP-25-0317), limits the secondary overcurrent device for a transformer over 1,000 V to 125% of the transformer secondary full-load current; the 250% column applies only where the transformer is supervised. ISA Article 4.1 requires the Facility to conform to the Company standards and the code in effect, and ISA Article 6.2 requires the AHJ's final approval of the customer's facilities.")
p("What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, dated 06/24/2025: the T-1 row states 750 kVA, 13.2 kV to 480Y/277 V and a full-load secondary current of 902 A; the SWBD-PV row states a 1,200 A bus and a 1,200 A main breaker. The calculation is 902 A × 1.25 = 1,127.6 A. The installed 1,200 A main is 133% of 902 A and 72.4 A (6.4%) above the 125% value. The record has no supervised-transformer designation, no signed supervision basis, no written next-higher-standard basis, and no AHJ finding specifically addressing the 125%/next-higher basis. The T-1 secondary cable bus rating is also not stated in the record. The 07/02/2025 Certificate of Final Approval records the inspection result but does not document these checks.")
p("Conclusion. On the strict, non-supervised reading of Table 450.3(A) — the reading I apply because the record does not establish supervision — the 1,200 A main exceeds the 125% secondary limit. I therefore cannot verify the T-1 secondary protection as designed. This is a hold item, not a documentation comment. If Corwyn contends that the next-higher standard rating is permitted, it must put the code basis and the AHJ's written acceptance on the record; the record as it stands does not contain either.")
p("What has to be done. Corwyn Realty Partners, through its contractor Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must do one of the following:", bold=False)
bullet("(a) Replace the SWBD-PV main breaker with a standard 1,000 A breaker (1,000 A / 902 A = 111%, within 125%), update the equipment schedule and the arc-flash label, and obtain re-inspection and final approval from the City of Wrenford; or")
bullet("(b) Provide a signed supervised-transformer basis acceptable to the City of Wrenford under Table 450.3(A), with the AHJ's written acceptance, and update the record accordingly; or")
bullet("(c) Provide the written code basis, and the City of Wrenford's written acceptance, for using the next-higher standard rating under Table 450.3(A) (1,200 A is the next standard rating above 1,127.6 A), and update the record accordingly. The record as it stands contains none of (a), (b) or (c).")
p("The replacement breaker must be rated for the 15.7 kA available fault current and the 35 kA switchboard rating, and the busbar check must remain satisfied: five 225 A inverter breakers plus the 40 A TX-1 breaker = 1,165 A, which is within the 1,200 A bus. The revised equipment schedule must also state the T-1 secondary cable bus rating and show that the 1,000 A (or documented 1,200 A) main protects it.")
p("Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor) for the design, breaker, cable-bus rating, code basis and AHJ submission; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for re-inspection and final approval; the DER Program Office for verification. Distribution Protection Engineering's POI settings and coordination study remain outside this memo; the DER Program Office will notify DPE of the corrected customer-side record for information only.")
p("Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Not on the record. As of 07/14/2025 there is no revised drawing, no breaker order or availability confirmation, no signed supervision/next-higher basis, no T-1 secondary cable-bus rating, and no AHJ re-inspection booked; the 07/02/2025 final approval is for the 1,200 A design. A 1,000 A breaker and a re-inspection, or a written code/AHJ basis, may be achievable in the time available, but the record does not demonstrate it. To keep 08/04/2025, Corwyn must complete (a), (b) or (c) and deliver the AHJ acceptance to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025. Otherwise PTO should be held and re-determined when the corrected record is complete. The witness test remains valid; the corrections do not require re-testing the inverter protective functions.")

'''
s=s[:start]+new_sec+s[end:]

# Update basis table statuses
s=s.replace('Complete and valid for the inverter protective functions. The main-breaker correction in F-1 does not require re-running the witness test.',
            'Complete and valid for the inverter protective functions. The AC conductor and main-breaker corrections in F-1/F-2 do not require re-running the witness test.')
s=s.replace('Issued, but it approves the 1,200 A main-breaker design and does not cure F-1. F-1 requires re-inspection/re-approval of the corrected design.',
            'Issued, but it approves the 4/0 AC conductor and 1,200 A main-breaker design and does not cure F-1 or F-2. Both require re-inspection/re-approval of the corrected design.')

# Add AC/DC circuits row to items table after Inverter certification
old='''        ("Inverter certification", "Vexlar VX-140C, five units, serials VX140C-25-03311, -03312, -03315, -03318 and -03320; certificate VX-CC-25-0522 dated 05/22/2025, UL 1741 including Supplement SB, IEEE 1547-2018 Category III; CEL-2025-Q2 row 18."),
        ("AHJ approval",'''
new='''        ("Inverter certification", "Vexlar VX-140C, five units, serials VX140C-25-03311, -03312, -03315, -03318 and -03320; certificate VX-CC-25-0522 dated 05/22/2025, UL 1741 including Supplement SB, IEEE 1547-2018 Category III; CEL-2025-Q2 row 18."),
        ("AC/DC circuits", "AC inverter output circuits are F-1. The DC output circuits pass the same 40 °C/75 °C check: 4/0 PV wire has 202.4 A corrected ampacity, above the 200 A fuse and the 157.5 A required; 10 AWG string conductors have 30.8 A corrected ampacity, above the 25 A fuse and the 17.5 A required."),
        ("AHJ approval",'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:

            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0

- **Owner:** Corwyn Realty Partners through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317).

[P1] 1. Determination
[P2] Permission to Operate cannot issue for Corwyn Office Complex PV on 08/04/2025 on the record before me. Two record items stand in the way. F-3: the PV labeling record does not demonstrate the service-equipment rapid-shutdown plaque required by NEC 690.56(C), or the full dc power-source label content required by NEC 690.53. F-2: the T-1 secondary protection record does not state the secondary cable-bus rating or the SWBD-PV main breaker's trip-setting/next-size basis, so I cannot verify that the 1,200 A main protects the secondary cable bus. The City of Wrenford's 07/02/2025 final approval and the 07/08/2025 witness test do not supply either record.
[P3] I have rechecked the two items the earlier record treated as code violations. The five 4/0 AWG Cu AC inverter output circuits are adequate: 236.6 A at 40 °C in the 90 °C column, capped at the 230 A 75 °C terminal rating under NEC 110.14(C)(1)(b)(2), is above the 225 A breaker and the 210 A required by 690.8. The 1,200 A SWBD-PV main is the next standard rating above 1,127.6 A and is permitted by the Table 450.3(A) next-higher-standard-rating note where the calculated value is not a standard rating and the device is a fuse or nonadjustable breaker; if the main is adjustable, its trip setting must be not more than 1,127.6 A. Neither item requires conductor or breaker replacement.
[P4] PTO can issue on 08/04/2025 only if F-2 and F-3 close and the pre-issuance confirmations below are completed: C-1 (VX-140C remains on CEL-2025-Q3, due 07/31/2025), C-2 (live telemetry at issuance) and C-4 (meter seal). The action deadline is 08/01/2025. If any remains open, PTO remains on hold and the Office will re-determine when the record is complete. The witness test remains valid; no inverter protective-function re-test is required for the label or record corrections.
[P5] 2. Basis: the ISA conditions and the record at 07/14/2025
[P6] ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, Article 6.2, permits parallel operation only once four conditions are met: (i) the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted; (ii) telemetry is live at the System Operations Center; (iii) the witness test is complete; and (iv) the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities. Article 4.1 also requires the Facility to conform to DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's Certified Equipment List, each as in effect from time to time. The facility is a 700 kW ac commercial small-scale DER (500 kW–1 MW), DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 Category 2; DPS-07 §4.2 separately requires the utility-owned POI recloser, which the checklist records as installed and accepted. The executed ISA and APUC Tariff §12.6 require the Company's written PTO before parallel operation. I checked each condition against the record as of 07/14/2025.
[P7] The four matters placed under separate review are not decided here: (1) the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser; (2) the POI recloser settings and the protection coordination study; (3) the site's queue position; and (4) the system impact study and its conditions. The checklist's entries for (1) and (2) are recorded as complete/accepted/issued on 07/08/2025 and 06/18/2025; I have not re-reviewed the underlying tests, settings or study. Nothing else is outside this memo.
[P8] 3. Findings: F-1 acceptable; F-2 and F-3 stand in the way
[P9] F-1. AC inverter output conductor ampacity — reviewed and found acceptable; not a hold.
[P10] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023 Sections 690.8(A)(1) and 690.8(B) require the inverter output conductors to carry 125% of the inverter continuous output current (1.25 × 168 A = 210 A) and to be protected by the 225 A breaker (NEC 240.4). Section 110.14(C)(1)(b)(2) permits higher-temperature conductors for circuits over 100 A, provided the ampacity does not exceed the 75 °C ampacity of the conductor; Section 310.15(B)(1) requires the 40 °C ambient correction.
[P11] What it rests on. Canopy Cable Schedule E-201 Rev C (06/24/2025), rows AC-C1 to AC-C5: 3 × 1/C 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2 plus 1/C 4 AWG Cu ground, 225 A breaker at SWBD-PV, inverter output 168 A; the schedule columns are “Ampacity at 40 °C, 90 °C column 236.6 A” and “Terminal rating 75 °C 230 A”; lengths are 96 to 160 m and voltage drop 1.16% to 1.93%.
[P12] Calculation. The 90 °C ampacity corrected to 40 °C is 260 × 0.91 = 236.6 A. The 110.14(C)(1)(b)(2) cap is the 75 °C ampacity, 230 A. The governing ampacity is therefore min(236.6, 230) = 230 A. That is above the 225 A breaker and above the 210 A required by 690.8. Utilisation is 225/230 = 0.978 against the breaker and 210/230 = 0.913 against the 690.8 minimum. The earlier 202.4 A result came from applying the 0.88 ambient correction to the already-75 °C-limited 230 A value; that is a second temperature reduction that 110.14(C)(1)(b)(2) does not require, because the 40 °C correction is already in the 236.6 A 90 °C value and the 230 A is the terminal cap.
[P13] Conclusion. The five 4/0 circuits and 225 A breakers comply. No conductor upsize, breaker change, written AHJ acceptance or AHJ re-inspection is required for F-1. The 225 A breaker also cannot be reduced to 200 A, because 690.8 requires at least 210 A.
[P14] F-2. T-1 secondary protection record — incomplete; the 1,200 A main is not a 125% violation.
[P15] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023 Table 450.3(A) (adopted by the City of Wrenford by Ordinance 24-118 and made part of permit WEP-25-0317) limits the secondary overcurrent device for a transformer over 1,000 V with a secondary of 1,000 V or less to 125% of the transformer secondary full-load current (1,127.6 A here). The table's next-higher-standard-rating note permits the next higher standard rating where the calculated value does not correspond to a standard rating of a fuse or nonadjustable circuit breaker; 1,200 A is that next standard rating (NEC 240.6(A)). If the main is an adjustable breaker, its trip setting must be not more than 1,127.6 A (NEC 240.6(C)). NEC 240.4 separately requires the secondary cable bus to be protected at its ampacity.
[P16] What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, dated 06/24/2025: the T-1 row states 750 kVA, 13.2 kV to 480Y/277 V, a full-load secondary current of 902 A and “secondary cable bus to SWBD-PV,” with no cable-bus rating or conductor size. The SWBD-PV row states a 1,200 A bus and a 1,200 A main breaker, but not whether the main is fixed or adjustable and not its trip setting.
[P17] Calculation. 902 A × 1.25 = 1,127.6 A. The installed 1,200 A main is 133% of 902 A and 1,200/1,127.6 = 1.064 of the 125% value. Because 1,127.6 A is not a standard rating, the next-size note permits 1,200 A for a fuse or nonadjustable breaker. For an adjustable breaker, setting it at 1,127.6 A gives 1,127.6/1,200 = 0.94 of the frame rating. The 1.064 ratio is therefore not a code violation.
[P18] Conclusion. The 1,200 A main is acceptable on the record's 902 A transformer, but I cannot verify the secondary cable-bus protection or the main trip setting. Those are the record gaps, not the 133% ratio.
[P19] What has to be done. Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must provide:
[P20] (a) the T-1 secondary cable-bus rating and ampacity, with the protection basis showing that the 1,200 A main (or a lower adjustable setting) protects it; if the cable bus is rated below 1,200 A, state the reduced setting or the cable-bus upgrade; and
[P21] (b) the SWBD-PV main breaker datasheet or setting record showing either a nonadjustable 1,200 A device, or an adjustable device set at not more than 1,127.6 A; and
[P22] (c) a revised E-101 or a signed supplement recording (a) and (b).
[P23] No breaker replacement is required unless the cable-bus rating is below 1,200 A and cannot be protected by a reduced setting. A record-only clarification does not require AHJ re-inspection; if the cable-bus rating requires a field change, the City's re-inspection follows. Distribution Protection Engineering's POI settings and coordination study are unaffected and remain under separate review; no DPE notification is required because the POI settings do not change.
[P24] Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor) for the cable-bus rating, breaker setting record and revised schedule; the DER Program Office for verification; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections only if a field change is required.
[P25] Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Yes if it is document-only: the cable-bus rating and breaker setting can be supplied by 08/01/2025. If the cable-bus rating is below 1,200 A and a field change is needed, the record does not demonstrate completion by 08/04/2025 and PTO should be held.
[P26] F-3. PV labeling record — incomplete; this is a record gap, not a proven field nonconformance.
[P27] Requirement. NFPA 70-2023 Section 690.56(C) requires a permanent plaque at the service equipment identifying the rapid shutdown system and its initiation device. Section 690.53 requires the dc power source label to give the maximum voltage, maximum current, maximum rated output current and maximum rated output power of the dc source. Section 690.12 contains the rapid shutdown requirements and the marking of the initiation device. The permit adopts NFPA 70-2023.
[P28] What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, Labels row: arc-flash labels, the SWBD-PV voltage/fault-current/clearing-time label, source-location plaques at SWBD-PV and PSW-1, the AD-C inverter-disconnect labels, the SWBD-PV main PV-system-disconnect label, and dc power source labels “giving the maximum dc voltage, 958.6 V.” The row does not record a rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment, and the dc labels do not record maximum current, maximum rated output current or maximum rated output power. String Schedule E-301 records module-level rapid shutdown devices, the transmitter at SWBD-PV and the initiator at the SWBD-PV main, but no service-equipment plaque.
[P29] Conclusion. The record does not demonstrate the required rapid shutdown plaque or the full dc label content. The installed labels may exist, but no inspection record in the file shows them; I therefore cannot verify compliance. This is a record gap, not a proven field defect.
[P30] What to do. Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-0317), must install or verify the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment identifying the system and its initiation device, complete the dc power source labels with the values required by Section 690.53, mark the initiation device if not already marked, and provide a photographed as-built label record. The City of Wrenford is to confirm the labels at re-inspection. The DER Program Office verifies the record.
[P31] Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners and Brantley Electric Company for the labels; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for inspection/confirmation; the DER Program Office for verification.
[P32] Can it be done before 08/04/2025? The field work can be done in a day and does not require conductor or breaker changes. The AHJ confirmation path is not on the record: the City issued final approval on 07/02/2025 and the file contains no post-final-approval re-inspection booking or process. Corwyn must confirm a City booking by 07/18/2025 and deliver the as-built label record and City confirmation to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025. If the City will not reopen or re-inspect, the labels can still be installed and photographed, but the 08/04/2025 date is not demonstrated; PTO may slip until the AHJ record is complete.
[P33] 4. Pre-issuance confirmations (to be closed before PTO)
[P34] C-1. CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025.
[P35] ISA Article 4.1 requires conformity with the Certified Equipment List as in effect from time to time. CEL-2025-Q2 (04/30/2025) lists VX-140C at row 18 and is the edition checked on the 07/14/2025 checklist. CEL-2025-Q2 states that CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025, before the requested PTO date. Evan Solberg, Standards Engineering, is to confirm in writing by 08/01/2025 that VX-140C remains listed on the CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025. If it is delisted, the facility cannot be verified against the current CEL and PTO must be held and re-determined; if it remains listed, this condition is closed. This confirmation can be completed by 08/01/2025.
[P36] C-2. Live telemetry at the moment of PTO.
[P37] TCS-02 §5 and ISA Articles 6.2 and 7.2 require live telemetry at the SOC when PTO is issued, with the SOC Shift Supervisor's confirmation recorded against the file. The checklist records the 07/08/2025 confirmation by L. Kovalchuk, and the 07/14/2025 SOC PTO-Hold Log has no Corwyn entry. Lena Kovalchuk/SOC is to re-confirm at the moment of issuance on 08/04/2025 that all required points are valid (not stale, forced or bad-quality) at the SCADA operator display. The 07/08/2025 confirmation is evidence for the record, not a substitute for the §5 confirmation at issuance. This confirmation can be completed at issuance on 08/04/2025.
[P38] C-3. First parallel operation.
[P39] ISA Article 6.3 and DPS-07 §6.3 require the first parallel operation after PTO to be observed by the SOC with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision. This is an operating step after PTO; it does not bar issuance and does not need to be completed before 08/04/2025, but it must be scheduled and recorded by the SOC.
[P40] C-4. Revenue meter seal.
[P41] ISA Article 7.1 requires the revenue-quality bidirectional meter at the POI to be owned, installed, tested and maintained by the Company and “sealed at all times.” The checklist records RM-0629 as set and tested and the delivered and received registers verified on 07/08/2025, but it does not record the seal. Alleniom Metering (Company) is to confirm the seal is installed and record the seal number before or at issuance on 08/04/2025. This is a field confirmation that can be completed at issuance; PTO should not issue without it.
[P42] 5. Line review of the customer's installation records
[P43] I reviewed the Corwyn equipment, cable, string and monitoring schedules against the NEC articles the City of Wrenford permit adopts (NFPA 70-2023) and against DIS-01, DPS-07 and TCS-02. The table records the result for each line, including the items that are not verified.
[P44] Record limitations disclosed by the line review. E-101 does not dimension the inverter working space or state whether the SWBD-PV main is lockable open; the 13.2 kV primary conductor size is not in the DER Program record and is covered by DPE's separate DER-side protection review. The City's 07/02/2025 final approval covers the installed NEC conditions. These are disclosed, not treated as separate utility holds; if the Office requires independent dimensional verification, it should obtain the as-built layout before issuance.
[P45] Other items reviewed and found acceptable
[P46] Other ISA terms. ISA Article 11.3 requires the Interconnection Customer to maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and to provide a certificate of that insurance on the Company's request. No certificate is in the file and no request is recorded; this is not a PTO condition and I have not treated it as a hold. If a certificate has been requested, it should be obtained before issuance.
[P47] 6. Scope and exclusions
[P48] This memo does not review or decide the four matters under separate review: (1) the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser at the site (SCADA/EMS Engineering and Distribution Protection Engineering); (2) the POI recloser's settings and the protection coordination study behind them (Distribution Protection Engineering, which issued them and keeps them outside these records); (3) the site's queue position (Meera Vellanki, under the weekly queue reports); and (4) the system impact study and its conditions (Ivo Grantham's DER Planning Group, which keeps them outside these records). Nothing else is excluded.
[P49] The RTU station-service/UPS ride-through is part of the RTU installation and configuration under separate review. I have not analyzed or relied on it. The checklist's statements that the RTU/POI recloser tests were accepted, that the POI recloser settings and coordination study were issued, and that the site is in commissioning are noted for context only. They are not a determination by this memo, and I have not re-reviewed the underlying tests, settings or study.
[P50] 7. Recommendation and next steps
[P51] Hold PTO for 08/04/2025. Do not issue PTO on the record as it stands.
[P52] Issue the Office's written notice to Corwyn Realty Partners (attention Nadia Ferreira-Holt) and Brantley Electric Company on 07/15/2025, stating F-2 (T-1 secondary cable-bus rating and SWBD-PV main trip-setting/next-size record) and F-3 (PV labeling record) and the 08/01/2025 deadline. State expressly that F-1 (4/0 AC conductors) and the 1,200 A SWBD-PV main are accepted and that no conductor or breaker replacement is required.
[P53] Corwyn/Brantley to deliver the F-2 cable-bus rating and breaker setting record and the F-3 as-built label record, with City of Wrenford confirmation, to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025.
[P54] Evan Solberg, Standards Engineering, to confirm the CEL-2025-Q3 listing of VX-140C by 08/01/2025 (C-1).
[P55] Lena Kovalchuk/SOC to re-confirm live telemetry at the moment of issuance on 08/04/2025 (C-2), and to schedule the first parallel operation observation under ISA Article 6.3 (C-3).
[P56] Alleniom Metering to confirm the revenue meter seal and record the seal number before or at issuance on 08/04/2025 (C-4).
[P57] If F-2, F-3 and C-1 are closed and C-2 and C-4 are confirmed, the Office may issue PTO on 08/04/2025. If any remains open, PTO remains on hold and the Office will re-determine when the record is complete. The witness test remains valid; no re-test of the inverter protective functions is required for the label or record corrections.

# Deliverable checklist — Corwyn PTO memo task

## Primary deliverable
- Path/name: `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx` (exact).
- Format: Word DOCX, memorandum to Lena Kovalchuk, SOC Shift Supervisor, from the DER Program Office reviewing engineer (P.E.).
- Date: 07/14/2025 (record as-of date).
- Project: Corwyn Office Complex PV, PXA-2023-0629, feeder ALN-072, 700 kW ac, ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex executed 09/12/2024.
- Decision date: 08/04/2025 (customer request of 07/10/2025).
- First answer: yes or no, one way or the other, with decisive reason.
- Basis: each ISA 6.2 PTO condition checked and cited (Company facilities commissioned/accepted; telemetry live at SOC; witness test complete; AHJ final approval).
- Every obstacle/finding: what it is; the requirement and clause/edition it rests on; the record evidence; what must be done; by whom (including Corwyn Realty Partners if customer-side); whether it can be done before 08/04/2025; consequence if not.
- Scope exclusions exactly: (1) RTU/POI recloser installation, configuration and commissioning tests (SCADA/EMS and Distribution Protection Engineering); (2) POI recloser settings and protection coordination study (DPE, outside records); (3) site queue position (Meera Vellanki, weekly queue reports); (4) system impact study and conditions (Ivo Grantham/DER Planning Group, outside records). Nothing else excluded.
- Items reviewed and acceptable, briefly.
- Recommendation/next steps with dates.
- Signature block for reviewing engineer (P.E.), no invented name/credentials.
- Do not use documents dated after 07/14/2025; do not rely on superseded/cancelled docs.

## Work package
- Open exactly one work package in OpenProject project "DER Program Backlog Review" (project id 3).
- Record the determination (PTO can/cannot issue 08/04/2025) and every pre-PTO item, owner, due date, including Corwyn Realty Partners.
- Read it back and verify fields/content.

## Supporting files (internal, for grading method)
- `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv` — hard requirements with candidate IDs.
- `/tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv` — rejected candidates/document reasons.
- `/tmp/ahpele/asks.md` — every instruction ask.

- Run `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_reqscan.py --register /tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv` and `--check`.

## Key values to reconcile in memo
- ISA capacity 700 kW ac; T-1 750 kVA; T-1 480 V secondary FLA 902 A; SWBD-PV 1,200 A bus / 1,200 A main; five 225 A inverter breakers + 40 A TX-1 = 1,165 A.
