The four matters placed under separate review are not decided here: (1) the installation,
configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser; (2) the POI
recloser settings and the protection coordination study; (3) the site's queue position; and (4)
the system impact study and its conditions. The checklist's entries for (1) and (2) are
recorded as complete/accepted/issued on 07/08/2025 and 06/18/2025; I have not re-
reviewed the underlying tests, settings or study. Nothing else is outside this memo.

3. Findings: F-1 acceptable; F-2 and F-3 stand in the way
F-1. AC inverter output conductor ampacity — reviewed and found acceptable; not a
hold.
Requirement. NFPA 70-2023 Sections 690.8(A)(1) and 690.8(B) require the inverter output
conductors to carry 125% of the inverter continuous output current (1.25 × 168 A = 210 A)
and to be protected by the 225 A breaker (NEC 240.4). Section 110.14(C)(1)(b)(2) permits
higher-temperature conductors for circuits over 100 A, provided the ampacity does not
exceed the 75 °C ampacity of the conductor; Section 310.15(B)(1) requires the 40 °C
ambient correction.
What it rests on. Canopy Cable Schedule E-201 Rev C (06/24/2025), rows AC-C1 to AC-C5: 3
× 1/C 4/0 AWG Cu THHN/THWN-2 plus 1/C 4 AWG Cu ground, 225 A breaker at SWBD-PV,
inverter output 168 A; the schedule columns are “Ampacity at 40 °C, 90 °C column 236.6 A”
and “Terminal rating 75 °C 230 A”; lengths are 96 to 160 m and voltage drop 1.16% to
1.93%.
Calculation. The 90 °C ampacity corrected to 40 °C is 260 × 0.91 = 236.6 A. The 110.14(C)
(1)(b)(2) cap is the 75 °C ampacity, 230 A. The governing ampacity is therefore min(236.6,
230) = 230 A. That is above the 225 A breaker and above the 210 A required by 690.8.
Utilisation is 225/230 = 0.978 against the breaker and 210/230 = 0.913 against the 690.8
minimum. The earlier 202.4 A result came from applying the 0.88 ambient correction to the
already-75 °C-limited 230 A value; that is a second temperature reduction that 110.14(C)(1)
(b)(2) does not require, because the 40 °C correction is already in the 236.6 A 90 °C value
and the 230 A is the terminal cap.
Conclusion. The five 4/0 circuits and 225 A breakers comply. No conductor upsize, breaker
change, written AHJ acceptance or AHJ re-inspection is required for F-1. The 225 A breaker
also cannot be reduced to 200 A, because 690.8 requires at least 210 A.
F-2. T-1 secondary protection record — incomplete; the 1,200 A frame is not a 125%
violation, but the trip setting and cable-bus rating are not verified.
Requirement. NFPA 70-2023 Table 450.3(A) (adopted by the City of Wrenford by Ordinance
24-118 and made part of permit WEP-25-0317) limits the secondary overcurrent device for a
transformer over 1,000 V with a secondary of 1,000 V or less to 125% of the transformer
secondary full-load current (1,127.6 A here). The table's next-higher-standard-rating note
permits the next higher standard rating where the calculated value does not correspond to a
standard rating of a fuse or nonadjustable circuit breaker; 1,200 A is that next standard
rating (NEC 240.6(A)). If the main is an adjustable breaker, its trip setting must be not more
than 1,127.6 A (NEC 240.6(B)/(C)). NEC 240.4 separately requires the secondary cable bus
to be protected at its ampacity.

         Corwyn Office Complex PV (PXA-2023-0629) — PTO determination | 07/14/2025 | Page 3 of 10
                                                Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office | Internal Memorandum

What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, dated 06/24/2025: the T-1 row states
750 kVA, 13.2 kV to 480Y/277 V, a full-load secondary current of 902 A and “secondary
cable bus to SWBD-PV,” with no cable-bus rating or conductor size. The SWBD-PV row
states a 1,200 A bus and a 1,200 A main breaker, but not whether the main is fixed or
adjustable and not its trip setting.
Calculation. 902 A × 1.25 = 1,127.6 A. The installed 1,200 A main is 133% of 902 A and
1,200/1,127.6 = 1.064 of the 125% value. Because 1,127.6 A is not a standard rating, the
next-size note permits 1,200 A for a fuse or nonadjustable breaker. For an adjustable
breaker, setting it at 1,127.6 A gives 1,127.6/1,200 = 0.94 of the frame rating. The 1.064
ratio is therefore not a code violation.
Conclusion. The 1,200 A frame is acceptable on the next-size basis if the device is
nonadjustable; if it is adjustable, it is acceptable only with a setting not more than 1,127.6 A.
I cannot verify which, or the secondary cable-bus protection. Those are the record gaps, not
the 133% ratio.
What has to be done. Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company (permit
WEP-25-0317), must provide:
  (a) the T-1 secondary cable-bus rating and ampacity, with the protection basis showing
   that the 1,200 A main (or a lower adjustable setting) protects it; if the cable bus is rated
   below 1,200 A, state the reduced setting or the cable-bus upgrade; and
 (b) the SWBD-PV main breaker datasheet or setting record showing either a
   nonadjustable 1,200 A device, or an adjustable device set at not more than 1,127.6 A;
   and
 (c) a revised E-101 or a signed supplement recording (a) and (b).
No breaker replacement is required unless the cable-bus rating is below 1,200 A and cannot
be protected by a reduced setting. A record-only clarification does not require AHJ re-
inspection; if the cable-bus rating requires a field change, the City's re-inspection follows.
Distribution Protection Engineering's POI settings and coordination study are unaffected
and remain under separate review; no DPE notification is required if the main remains a
nonadjustable 1,200 A device. If the setting is changed, the DER Program Office will notify
DPE for information.
Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners (owner) and Brantley Electric Company (contractor)
for the cable-bus rating, breaker setting record and revised schedule; the DER Program
Office for verification; the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections only if a field change
is required.
Can it be done before 08/04/2025? Yes if it is document-only: the cable-bus rating and
breaker setting can be supplied by 08/01/2025. If the cable-bus rating is below 1,200 A and
a field change is needed, the record does not demonstrate completion by 08/04/2025 and
PTO should be held.
F-3. PV labeling record — incomplete; this is a record gap, not a proven field
nonconformance.
Requirement. NFPA 70-2023 Section 690.56(C) requires a permanent plaque at the service
equipment identifying the rapid shutdown system and its initiation device. Section 690.53
requires the dc power source label to give the maximum voltage, maximum current,
maximum rated output current and maximum rated output power of the dc source. Section
690.12 contains the rapid shutdown requirements and the marking of the initiation device.
The permit adopts NFPA 70-2023.
What it rests on. Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C, Labels row: arc-flash labels, the SWBD-
PV voltage/fault-current/clearing-time label, source-location plaques at SWBD-PV and
PSW-1, the AD-C inverter-disconnect labels, the SWBD-PV main PV-system-disconnect label,
and dc power source labels “giving the maximum dc voltage, 958.6 V.” The row does not

         Corwyn Office Complex PV (PXA-2023-0629) — PTO determination | 07/14/2025 | Page 4 of 10
                                                Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office | Internal Memorandum

record a rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment, and the dc labels do not record
maximum current, maximum rated output current or maximum rated output power. String
Schedule E-301 records module-level rapid shutdown devices, the transmitter at SWBD-PV
and the initiator at the SWBD-PV main, but no service-equipment plaque.
Conclusion. The record does not demonstrate the required rapid shutdown plaque or the full
dc label content. The installed labels may exist, but no inspection record in the file shows
them; I therefore cannot verify compliance. This is a record gap, not a proven field defect.
What to do. Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company (permit WEP-25-
0317), must install or verify the rapid shutdown plaque at the service equipment identifying
the system and its initiation device, complete the dc power source labels with the values
required by Section 690.53, mark the initiation device if not already marked, and provide a
photographed as-built label record. The City of Wrenford is to confirm the labels at re-
inspection. The DER Program Office verifies the record.
Who does it. Corwyn Realty Partners and Brantley Electric Company for the labels; the City
of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) for
inspection/confirmation; the DER Program Office for verification.
Can it be done before 08/04/2025? The field work can be done in a day and does not require
conductor or breaker changes. The AHJ confirmation path is not on the record: the City
issued final approval on 07/02/2025 and the file contains no post-final-approval re-inspection
booking or process. Corwyn must confirm a City booking by 07/18/2025 and deliver the as-
built label record and City confirmation to the DER Program Office by 08/01/2025. If the
City will not reopen or re-inspect, the labels can still be installed and photographed, but the
08/04/2025 date is not demonstrated; PTO may slip until the AHJ record is complete.

4. Pre-issuance confirmations (to be closed before PTO)
C-1. CEL edition in force on 08/04/2025.
ISA Article 4.1 requires conformity with the Certified Equipment List as in effect from time
to time. CEL-2025-Q2 (04/30/2025) lists VX-140C at row 18 and is the edition checked on
the 07/14/2025 checklist. CEL-2025-Q2 states that CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025,
before the requested PTO date. Evan Solberg, Standards Engineering, is to confirm in
writing by 08/01/2025 that VX-140C remains listed on the CEL edition in force on
08/04/2025. If it is delisted, the facility cannot be verified against the current CEL and PTO
must be held and re-determined; if it remains listed, this condition is closed. This
confirmation can be completed by 08/01/2025.
C-2. Live telemetry at the moment of PTO.
TCS-02 §5 and ISA Articles 6.2 and 7.2 require live telemetry at the SOC when PTO is
issued, with the SOC Shift Supervisor's confirmation recorded against the file. The checklist
records the 07/08/2025 confirmation by L. Kovalchuk, and the 07/14/2025 SOC PTO-Hold
Log has no Corwyn entry. Lena Kovalchuk/SOC is to re-confirm at the moment of issuance
on 08/04/2025 that all required points are valid (not stale, forced or bad-quality) at the
SCADA operator display. The 07/08/2025 confirmation is evidence for the record, not a
substitute for the §5 confirmation at issuance. This confirmation can be completed at
issuance on 08/04/2025.
C-3. First parallel operation.
ISA Article 6.3 and DPS-07 §6.3 require the first parallel operation after PTO to be observed
by the SOC with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision. This is an operating step after
PTO; it does not bar issuance and does not need to be completed before 08/04/2025, but it
must be scheduled and recorded by the SOC.
C-4. Revenue meter seal.


         Corwyn Office Complex PV (PXA-2023-0629) — PTO determination | 07/14/2025 | Page 5 of 10
                                                       Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office | Internal Memorandum

ISA Article 7.1 requires the revenue-quality bidirectional meter at the POI to be owned,
installed, tested and maintained by the Company and “sealed at all times.” The checklist
records RM-0629 as set and tested and the delivered and received registers verified on

seal is installed and record the seal number before or at issuance on 08/04/2025. This is a

[P1] 1. Determination
[P2] Permission to Operate cannot issue for Corwyn Office Complex PV on 08/04/2025 on the record before me. Two record items stand in the way. F-3: the PV labeling record does not demonstrate the service-equipment rapid-shutdown plaque required by NEC 690.56(C), or the full dc power-source label content required by NEC 690.53. F-2: the T-1 secondary protection record does not state the secondary cable-bus rating or the SWBD-PV main breaker's trip-setting/next-size basis, so I cannot verify that the 1,200 A main protects the secondary cable bus. The City of Wrenford's 07/02/2025 final approval and the 07/08/2025 witness test do not supply either record.
[P3] I have rechecked the two items the earlier record treated as code violations. The five 4/0 AWG Cu AC inverter output circuits are adequate: 236.6 A at 40 °C in the 90 °C column, capped at the 230 A 75 °C terminal rating under NEC 110.14(C)(1)(b)(2), is above the 225 A breaker and the 210 A required by 690.8. The 1,200 A SWBD-PV main is the next standard rating above 1,127.6 A and is permitted by the Table 450.3(A) next-higher-standard-rating note where the calculated value is not a standard rating and the device is a fuse or nonadjustable breaker; if the main is adjustable, it must be a restricted-access adjustable device set at not more than 1,127.6 A. F-1 requires no conductor replacement. The 1,200 A main requires no breaker replacement if it is nonadjustable or a restricted-access adjustable device set at not more than 1,127.6 A; otherwise a 1,000 A main may be required.
[P4] PTO can issue on 08/04/2025 only if F-2 and F-3 close and the pre-issuance confirmations below are completed: C-1 (VX-140C remains on CEL-2025-Q3, due 07/31/2025), C-2 (live telemetry at issuance) and C-4 (meter seal). The action deadline is 08/01/2025. If any remains open, PTO remains on hold and the Office will re-determine when the record is complete. The witness test remains valid; no inverter protective-function re-test is required for the label or record corrections.
[P5] 2. Basis: the ISA conditions and the record at 07/14/2025
[P6] ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, Article 6.2, permits parallel operation only once four conditions are met: (i) the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted; (ii) telemetry is live at the System Operations Center; (iii) the witness test is complete; and (iv) the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities. Article 4.1 also requires the Facility to conform to DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's Certified Equipment List, each as in effect from time to time. The facility is a 700 kW ac commercial small-scale DER (500 kW–1 MW), DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 Category 2; DPS-07 §4.2 separately requires the utility-owned POI recloser, which the checklist records as installed and accepted. The executed ISA and APUC Tariff §12.6 require the Company's written PTO before parallel operation. I checked each condition against the record as of 07/14/2025.
[P7] The four matters placed under separate review are not decided here: (1) the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser; (2) the POI recloser settings and the protection coordination study; (3) the site's queue position; and (4) the system impact study and its conditions. The checklist's entries for (1) and (2) are recorded as complete/accepted/issued on 07/08/2025 and 06/18/2025; I have not re-reviewed the underlying tests, settings or study. Nothing else is outside this memo.
[P8] 3. Findings: F-1 acceptable; F-2 and F-3 stand in the way
